records.qtitle: Indifferent implementation of Reverse Mortgage Loan
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	the details of the representations received regarding Reverse Mortgage Loan (RML) and crux of the matter involved in the same; <br/>(b)	the details of the steps taken by Government to tackle the issue;<br/>(c)	whether Government is aware that senior citizens are still facing problem due to indifferent attitude of the concerned officers in implementation of the scheme; and <br/>(d)	how Government proposes to resolve the RML issue?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/>(a) to (d): Representations received regarding Reverse Mortgage Loan (RML) inter-alia include non sanction of loans by Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs), requests for rebate / concession in interest rate, requests for flexibility in term and tenure, modification in the guidelines etc. PLIs exercise discretion in designing their RML product and extend loans in accordance with their commercial judgment and risk perception within the framework provided by the RML scheme.<br/><br/>Government have taken various steps to improve effectiveness of the RML Scheme and reduce problems faced by senior citizens which inter-alia includes sensitizing banks that schemes designed for senior citizens be handled by Officers with proven track record of customer satisfaction, increasing public awareness through Public Sector Banks (PSBs), seminars / workshops / interactions with senior citizens at different centres by National Housing Bank (NHB), training programmes for officials of Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs), RML counselling centres in various cities in association with reputed Non Governmental Organizations (NGOs) to cater to the needs of senior citizen, Reverse Mortgage enabled Annuity (RMLeA) being made eligible for tax exemption etc.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Search and surveys conducted by IT Department
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) how many search and surveys have been taken up by the IT Department in the country during the last three years; <br/>(b) how many search and survey have been converted in raids during the same period; and <br/>(c) the actual amount of recovery and revenue generated to Government?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE<br/>(SHRI SHIV PRATAP SHUKLA)<br/><br/>(a): Details of the Financial Year-wise Search & Seizure and survey operations conducted by the Income-tax Department in the last three F.Ys. and the current F.Y., are as under:<br/>F.Y.	No. of groups searched	No. of Surveys conducted<br/>2014-15	545	5035<br/>2015-16	447	4428<br/>2016-17	1152	12520<br/>2017-18 (till Feb., 2018)	527	11120<br/>(b): Section 132 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 lays down the provisions relating to search and seizure operations. Under this section, the assessee’s premises are searched and seizure is made of undisclosed assets and incriminating documents. Under section 133A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 surveys are conducted in the business premises of the assessee and the documents/valuables found are inspected and verified. If deemed necessary, the documents may be impounded also. However, there is no mention of the term ‘raid’, in the Income-tax Act, 1961.<br/>(c): The Income-tax Department seizes the unexplained assets like cash, jewellery etc. found during the search and seizure operations. On the basis of the evidences gathered during search operation and the subsequent investigation, tax assessments are finalized and a tax demand is raised. However, the income assessed and the tax thereupon get crystallised conclusively only when appeals, if any, preferred before CIT(A), ITAT, High Court and Hon’ble Supreme Court are decided. Hence, the outcomes of the inquiry conducted and the actual amount of recovery and revenue generated to Government can be determined only after the finalization of these appeals.<br/>However, during the last three F.Y.s and the current F.Y. the total seizure and undisclosed income admitted during search and seizure actions is as under : - <br/>F.Y.	Total seizure (in Rs. Crores)	Undisclosed income admitted during search and seizure actions (in Rs. Crores)<br/>2014-15	761.70	10228.05<br/>2015-16	712.32	11226.02<br/>2016-17	1469.62	15496.73<br/>2017-18 (till Feb., 2018)	938.69	14038.89<br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Difference in average CDR of PSBs
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) the average Credit Deposit Ratio (CDR) of the Public Sector Banks (PSBs) during the current financial year till December, 2017; <br/>(b) whether there is a difference in the average CDR of PSBs in various States/UTs of the country;<br/>(c) if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise including Jharkhand and Gujarat; and<br/>(d) the steps taken by Government to minimise regional imbalances in credit deployment?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/>(a), (b) and (c): As per the information provided by the Reserve Bank of India, the overall  CD Ratio of all Public Sector Banks as at the end of December, 2017 stood at 69.56. A Statement indicating State/UT-wise (including Jharkhand and Gujarat) CD Ratio of Public Sector Banks during 2017-18 is Annexed.<br/> (d):  Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has advised the banks including PSBs to achieve a CDR of 60% in respect of their rural and semi-urban branches separately on an all India basis. The banks are required to ensure that wide disparity in the ratios between different State/Region is avoided in order to minimize regional imbalance in credit deployment. <br/>       RBI has also advised banks that the CD ratios should be monitored at different levels viz banks’ head office, State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC) and District Consultative Committee (DCC). Special Sub-Committee (SSC) of DCC is to be set up in the districts having CD ratio less than 40, in order to monitor the CD ratio and to draw up monitorable Action Plans (MAPs) to increase the CD ratio. The Districts with CD ratio less than 20 are treated on a special footing.<br/> ****<br/>

records.qtitle: Project Green Ports
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)   the objective, details and status of the proposed ‘Project Green Ports’ nation-wide;<br/>(b)   whether ports of Gujarat are covered under it, if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c)   the achievements of the project so far;<br/>(d)   whether procurement of the requisite equipments for monitoring environmental     pollution and dust suppression system has been completed and if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(e)  the financial implications involved in the execution of the said project and expenditure incurred so far?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: (a):  Under the Green Port Initiatives, the Ministry has identified 12 activities to make the Major Ports more clean and green from the environmental perspective for implementation by Major Ports.  A List of initiatives is annexed.<br/> <br/>(b) & (c): No. However, Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB) has started initiatives on its own for making their ports green for safe by providing dust suppression system and by monitoring of air pollution in the ports. Dust suppression system and Seawater treatment plant has already been installed in Navlakhi, Bhavnagar and Magadalla. In Mundra, diesel operated cranes has been converted to electric mode and 1.5 MW capacity solar panels has been installed. Regular Ambient Air Quality Monitoring in the GMB ports and Private Ports under the jurisdiction of GMB are being done.<br/><br/>(d)& (e): Under the Central Sector Scheme(CSS) financial assistance is provided to Major Ports and Oil Handling Non-Major Ports under the State Maritime Boards/State Governments for  procurement of equipments for Combating Oil Pollution and for mitigating measures. Assistance under the scheme is 50% of the total cost of the procurement of pollution response equipments/materials and the balance 50% are to be contributed by the respective port from its own resources subject to a maximum limit according to the categorization of port.  The total release of funds under the scheme is Rs. 19.24 crores so far.<br/><br/>	                            Annexure<br/><pre><br/>S.No	Name of Key Activity / Project	Name of Sub-Activities<br/>1	Green Port initiatives	Preparation of Environment Management & Monitoring Plan (EMMP) or Green Plan;<br/>2	-Do-	For acquiring equipments required for monitoring environmental pollution;<br/>3	-Do-	For acquiring dust suppression system;<br/>4	-Do-	For setting up of sewage / waste water treatment plants / garbage disposal plant;<br/>5	-Do-	For plantation;<br/>6	-Do-	For setting up projects for energy generation from renewable energy sources;<br/>7	-Do-	Use of bio-diesel and any other activity which is part of EMMP.<br/>8	-Do-	Completion of shortfalls of Oil Spill Response (OSR) facilities (Tier-I)<br/>9	-Do-	Improve Quality of Harbour Waters.<br/>10	-Do-	Implement of sustainable practices in Terminal Design, Development and Operations.<br/>11	-Do-	Prohibition of disposal of almost all kinds of garbages sea<br/>12	-Do-	Provision of adequate reception facilities in ships as per IMO guidelines & resolution<br/>                                               </pre><br/><br/>                       *****

records.qtitle: Promotion of S and T in the country
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: a)	the steps being taken by Government to promote Science and Technology (S&T) in the country; and<br/><br/>(b)	the details of funds allocated and utilized in various projects/programmes to promote S&T in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY, MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES AND MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE<br/>(DR. HARSH VARDHAN)<br/><br/>(a)	Government has taken several steps to promote Science and Technology (S&T) in the country. The S&T ecosystem is supported through targeted schemes focusing on strengthening human and institutional capacity for basic research and expanding R&D base; technology development and deployment; S&T co-operation / partnerships and alliances and societal interventions of S&T. While seeding and capacity building in the cutting-edge research areas to translational research; supporting innovation and startup ecosystem, and instituting new schemes and pripitous policy frameworks for public-private partneships, the Ministry has given special attention to align these activities with the national agenda of the Government towards Make in India, Startup India, Digital India, Swachh Bharat, Swasth Bharat, etc. The support system includes the extramural funding schemes and Fellowship schemes of Ministry of Science and Technology such as Fund for improvement of S&T infrastructures in universities and higher educational institutions (FIST), Core Research Grant, Nano Mission, Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE), Start-Up Grant for Young Scientists in the form of Early Career Research Award and National Postdoctoral Fellowship, Research fellowships such as JC Bose and Swarnajayanti, Thematic research support to Clean Energy and Water, Smart grids etc.<br/><br/>(b)	Funding for S&T promotion has been provided primarily in the form of R&D projects, research fellowships, mobility grant etc. to individual scientists and various institutions / agencies across the country. Budgetary allocation for scientific departments has constantly been increased year after year and the Ministry of Science and Technology allocated / utilized Rs. 27,184.35 crores in the last three years (2014-17) in various projects/programmes to promote S&T in the country.<br/><br/>                              ********<br/>

records.qtitle: Allocation of funds under DDUSY
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) 	the details of the proposed Deen Dayal Upadhyay Swaniyojan Yojana (DDUSY) under consideration of Government;<br/> <br/>(b) 	the modalities of the said scheme; <br/><br/>(c) 	whether any budgetary allocation has been made for the said scheme and if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(d) 	by when the said scheme is likely to be approved and implemented?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (d):	Ministry of Rural Development had prepared an proposal for scheme called Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Swaniyojan Yojana (DDU-GSY). The proposed scheme has now been merged in the Mission Antyodaya, which addresses convergence of schemes for alleviation of rural poverty and therefore a proposal for a separate DDU-GSY scheme stands closed.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Training institutions for sports promotion in the country
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) the State/UT-wise details of training institutions including provisions of sports education for promotion of sports in the country;<br/>(b) the details of various centrally sponsored schemes implemented for sports, sports education and training institutions in the country;<br/>(c) the present status of implementation of these schemes in Jharkhand and Gujarat and outcome thereof and the deficiencies identified therein: and<br/>(d) the remedial measures taken/proposed to be taken by Government for effective implementation of these schemes?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS<br/>[COL RAJYAVARDHAN RATHORE, AVSM (RETD.)]<br/><br/>(a) Sir, Such details are not centrally maintained as sports is a state subject. Sports being a state subject, the states have the primary responsibility for promotion and development of sports in their respective states. However, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and the Sports Authority of India supplement the efforts of the State Governments under their schemes aimed at broad-basing of sports and promotion, development and excellence in sports.<br/>(b) Presently, no ‘Centrally Sponsored Scheme’ is implemented in the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. All schemes being implemented are ‘Central Sector Schemes’.<br/>(c) & (d): In view of (b) above, questions do not arise.<br/>*****

records.qtitle: Promotion of conventions for attracting tourism
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government mulls to promote conventions in order to attract large scale tourism and if so, the details thereof; <br/>(b) 	which are the conventions which Government intends to promote nationally and internationally to attract tourism in Gujarat and Jharkhand; and <br/>(c) 	whether Government has issued any advisory to the State Governments to promote conventions in order to attract large scale tourism and if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR TOURISM (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>(SHRI K. J. ALPHONS)<br/><br/>(a) to (c):	Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Tourism promotes India as a holistic destination. The Ministry of Tourism has recognized Meetings, Incentives, Conventions and Exhibitions (MICE) as a ‘Niche Tourism’ product in order to overcome the aspect of ‘seasonality’ and to promote India as a 365 days’ destination and attract tourists with specific interests to India including the States of Gujarat and Jharkhand.  <br/><br/>The India Convention Promotion Bureau (ICPB) has been set up under the patronage of the Ministry of Tourism to promote India as a venue for International Conferences and Exhibitions. This non-profit organization, with members comprising national airlines, hotels, travel agents, tour operators, tourist transport operators, conference organizers, etc. participate in International MICE Tourism trade fairs like IMEX in Frankfurt and Las Vegas, EIBTM- Barcelona and AIME- Melbourne along with the Indiatourism overseas offices. India is also being promoted as a preferred MICE destination through the Global Incredible India media campaign and through Road Shows and Seminars conducted by the India Tourism offices overseas. Ministry of Tourism also provides Central Financial Assistance to the State Governments/UT Administrations for development of tourism infrastructure including the setting up of convention centres under the existing schemes.<br/><br/>*******<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Supply of rice to the poor under PDS
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text: (a) whether States/UTs possess flexibility to fix retail price of commodities under the Public Distribution System (PDS) considering local parameters;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof about Jharkhand along with the response and subsidy granted to Jharkhand and other States/UTs;<br/>(c) whether PDS has impacted country''s rice production and if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise during the last three years; and<br/>(d) the steps taken by Government for adequate supply of rice to the poor under PDS?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION<br/>(SHRI RAMVILAS PASWAN)<br/>(a) & (b): Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) is now implemented as per provisions of the National Food Security Act, 2013 (NFSA). Under the Act eligible households are entitled to receive foodgrains at subsidized prices specified in Schedule-I, i.e. not exceeding Rs.3/2/1 per kg for rice/wheat/coarsegrains. The difference between the Economic Cost of foodgrains and the above mentioned subsidized Central Issue Prices, is borne by the Central Government as food subsidy. At the current level of Economic Cost, the per unit subsidy for allocation of foodgrains out of Central pool stocks for eligible Antyodaya Anna Yojana and priority households, is Rs.29.94 per kg for rice and Rs.21.96 per kg for wheat.<br/>NFSA further provides that State Government may continue with or formulate food or nutrition based plans or schemes providing for benefits higher than the benefits provided under the Act. States/UTs therefore have the flexibility to further subsidise the foodgrains out of their own resources and distribute it at prices lower than the prices specified under the Act. Government of Jharkhand has informed that the end retail price under TPDS in the State is Rs.1 per kg for both wheat and rice.<br/>(c) & (d): For ensuring remunerative prices to farmers, Government procures wheat and paddy at Minimum Support Price. The foodgrains so procured is used for distribution of wheat and rice through TPDS, which is now implemented as per provisions of NFSA. The Act provides for coverage of 75% of rural and 50% of the urban population, at the all India level, for receiving highly subsidized foodgrains, corresponding to which State/UT-wise coverage was determined by the then Planning Commission. For the coverage of population determined for each State/UT, and identification of eligible households by States Governments/UT Administrations within that, the entitled quantities of wheat and rice are being supplied to States/UTs, for distribution among eligible households.<br/>The production of rice during 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2016-17 has been 105482.1 thousand tons, 104408.2 thousand tons and records.qtitle: Plan to reduce reliance on import of bulk drugs
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: <br/><br/>Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that Indian Pharmaceutical industry, which was a leading producer in bulk drugs, is becoming dependent on China for its bulk drug needs; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/>(c) whether Government has formulated any plan of action for reducing reliance of Indian Pharma sector on imports; and <br/>(d) if so, the details thereof along with the actual imports of bulk drugs during the last three years?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/><br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS; MINISTRY OF SHIPPING AND MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI MANSUKH L. MANDAVIYA)<br/><br/>(a): The country imports bulk drugs/Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) for producing medicines including certain essential medicines from China. As India is a signatory to the WTO and TRIPs agreement, as such the import restrictions have been removed. It may be mentioned that most of the imports of the Bulk Drug/APIs being done in the country are mainly because of economic considerations.<br/>(b) & (d): The details of India’s imports of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients as per Data available from the Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics (DGCIS), Kolkata is as under:<br/>Years	Total import<br/>(Rs. cr)	Imports from China<br/>(Rs. cr)<br/>2014-15	19833.19	14001.79<br/>2015-16	21225.97	13853.75<br/>2016-17	18372.54	12254.97<br/>As per DGCIS Kolkata, during the year 2016-17, the share of China in the total bulk drugs imported into the country was approximately 66 per cent.<br/>(c): The policies formulated by government from time to time are made so that the country’s dependence on imports are minimised. In this direction, the Government had on 28.01.2016 notified the withdrawal of exemption in customs duties which were earlier given to certain categories of drugs and bulk drugs to provide a boost to the domestic manufacturers. Further, the government has removed some bottlenecks in environment clearance etc. which the manufacturers were facing, in order to give a boost to domestic manufacturing of bulk drugs. Further, the Standing Finance Committee (SFC) has approved on 07.02.2018, the Scheme for ‘Development of Pharmaceutical Industry’ under which one of the components is for financing common facilities in Bulk Drug Parks. This would help in reducing the cost of production and would result in better availability of cheaper medicines for the patients. <br/>xxxxx <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Production of pulses
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the production of pulses in the country has been affected due to drought during the last three consecutive years, if so, the details thereof, State-wise; <br/><br/>(b)	 the steps taken by Government to increase the production of pulses; <br/><br/>(c) 	the names of States where the National Food Security Mission is being implemented; and <br/><br/>(d) 	the allocation made for increasing pulses production during the Financial Year 2018-19?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)<br/><br/>(a): 	On account of deficit /deficient rainfall during monsoon season, unseasonal rains/hailstorms and adverse temperature conditions etc., production of pulses during 2014-15 and 2015-16 declined to 17.15 million tonnes and 16.35 million tonnes, respectively as compared to their previous record production of 19.25 million tonnes in 2013-14. However, due to normal monsoon in 2016 and various measures taken by the Government, production of pulses increased to 23.13 million tonnes during 2016-17 in the country. <br/><br/>The State-wise details of production of pulses during the last three years i.e. from 2014-15 to 2016-17 in the country are given at Annexure.<br/><br/>(b): 	In order to increase the production of pulses, Government of India has been implementing various Crop Development Schemes / Programmes such as National Food Security Mission (NFSM)-Pulses, Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana, National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), Soil Health Card, etc. <br/><br/>Additional Area Coverage of Pulses during Rabi/Summer is a programme under NFSM-Pulses. The interventions covered under Additional Area Coverage of Pulses include demonstrations on improved technologies, distribution of certified seeds, effective water application tools, Integrated Nutrient Management (INM), Integrated Pest Management (IPM).<br/><br/>Further, to boost production of pulses in the country, Government has initiated various additional steps from the year 2016-17 which include creation of seed hubs through Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)/State Agricultural Universities (SAUs)/Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs); breeder seed production through ICAR institutes; distribution of seed minikits of pulses free of cost to farmers, incentives for seed production, etc.<br/><br/>The Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) of pulses have also been increased over the years to encourage farmers to grow more pulses by ensuring remunerative prices.<br/><br/>(c) & (d):	 National Food Security Mission (NFSM) is being implemented in 29 states i.e. Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tamilnadu, Telangana, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal.<br/><br/>A sum of Rs.1700/- crore has been earmarked for implementation of National Food Security Mission during 2018-19 (Budget Estimates) which includes the component of NFSM-Pulses.<br/>

records.qtitle: Reducing urban poverty
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of Housing & Urban Affairs be pleased to state:-<br/>a)	the details of reasons for increase in the rate of urban poverty;<br/>b)	the action taken by the Government to eliminate it;<br/>c)	whether more rural migrants and increasing birth rate in slums are causing urban poverty and if so, the details thereof; and<br/>d)	the initiatives taken by the Government to generate ample employment opportunities to reduce urban poverty?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF <br/>THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN AFFAIRS<br/>[SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI]<br/> <br/>(a) & (b) As per Poverty Estimates for 2011-12 released by the erstwhile Planning Commission, the percentage of persons below poverty line in 2011-12 has been estimated as 13.7% in urban areas. The corresponding estimates in 2004-05 and 1993-94 were 25.7% and 31.8% respectively. The average annual decline (percentage points per annum) in urban poverty ratio during the period 1993-94 to 2004-05 was 0.55, which accelerated to 1.69 during the period 2004-05 to 2011-12.<br/><br/>(c)	No data is available with the Ministry which supports the argument that rural migrants and increasing birth rate in slums is causing urban poverty.<br/><br/>(d)     This Ministry is implementing the “Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM)” to reduce poverty and vulnerability of urban poor households. The Mission provides skill training and placement in wage as well as self-employment. It also provides interest subvention on bank loans for self-employment ventures. <br/><br/>	Government has taken various steps for employment generation as well for improving employability. These include encouraging private sector, fast tracking various projects involving substantial investment and increasing public expenditure on Schemes like Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP). Government has also decided to strategically promote labour-intensive manufacturing and expand employment opportunities by promoting tourism and agro-based industries. The Make in India, Digital India, Skill India Schemes are being implemented by the Government to enhance the employment base. <br/>	A new Scheme Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) has been launched by the Government in the year 2016-17 for incentivising industry for promoting employment generation. <br/>                       *****<br/>

records.qtitle: High cost of electric vehicles
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) whether high cost of pure electric vehicles is a hurdle in its popularization and if so, the details thereof;<br/>(b) whether Government has formally launched the FAME India scheme incentivising electric and hybrid vehicles and if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(c) whether the Ministry has requested the Ministry of Finance to extend the 200 per cent incentives for research and development, especially for the automobile sector and if so, the details thereof?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER  OF  STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES (SHRI  BABUL SUPRIYO)<br/><br/> <br/>(a)	& (b): National Electric Mobility Mission Plan 2020 (NEMMP-2020) had flagged high cost of pure electric vehicles as one of the possible inhibiting factors.  Accordingly, demand incentives for electric and hybrid vehicles were included in the FAME India scheme as per ANNEXUTE 13 of the scheme’s Gazette Notification dated 13th march 2015 (S.O. No. 830(E)) and as amended from time to time, which are available at Department of Heavy Industry’s website (www.dhi.nic.in).<br/><br/>(c): No, Sir.<br/> <br/><br/>*********<br/>

records.qtitle: Setting up of heavy water reactors
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)   whether Government proposes to set up heavy water reactors in the country;<br/><br/>(b)   if so, the name of States where such reactors are proposed to be set up;<br/><br/>(c)   whether any assessment has been made regarding likely impact of the rising number of heavy water reactors on generation of electricity; and<br/><br/>(d)   if so, the details in this regard during the last three years?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS AND PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE (DR.JITENDRA SINGH):    <br/><br/>(a)	Yes, Sir. <br/><br/>(b)	At present, four indigenous Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) are under construction in the states of Gujarat (KAPP 3&4 - 2X700 MW) & Rajasthan (RAPP 7&8 – 2X700 MW). The Government has accorded administrative approval and financial sanction for setting up two more PHWRs in the State of Haryana (GHAVP 1&2 – 2X700 MW). In addition, the Government has accorded administrative approval and financial sanction for setting up ten indigenous 700 MW PHWRs in fleet mode, to be set up in the States of Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh & Karnataka.	<br/><br/>(c)	The present PHWR installed capacity is 4460 MW out of the total nuclear installed capacity of 6780 MW in the country. A PHWR installed capacity of 2800 MW is under construction and another 8400 MW has been accorded administrative approval and financial sanction. In addition, two Light Water Reactors (LWRs) of total 2000 MW capacity are under construction and two more of total 2000 MW capacity have been accorded administrative approval & financial sanction. This with PHWRs together would take total nuclear power installed capacity to 22480 MW by 2031 (including Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor [PFBR], 500 MW being implemented by BHAVINI). On their progressive completion, PHWRs along with LWRs are expected to contribute a significant portion of electricity to be generated from nuclear sources in the country in the near term.<br/><br/>(d)	The share of generation of electricity from PHWRs in the last three years is as follows:<br/>									                         (in million units)<br/>Year	                2014-15	     2015-16      2016-17<br/>Total Generation	         37835	      37456	  40001<br/>Generation from PHWRs	 31491	      33909	  29278<br/><br/><br/>****** <br/>

records.qtitle: Erecting new fence along India  Bangladesh border
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that India and Bangladesh have agreed to erect a new fence to secure over 250 villages ahead of the present barbed wire fencing along the international border to curb cross-border crimes; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c) whether the Border Security Force (BSF) and the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have signed an agreement in this regard; and <br/><br/>(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) to (d):	As per an agreement between the Government of India and the Government of Bangladesh no defence construction can be raised within 150 yards of the either side of International Border (IB) between India and Bangladesh. It is the endeavour of Government of India to erect border fence as close as possible to the IB so as to minimize dislocation of farmer/villagers/inhabitant. Based on the above lines, DG, Border Security Force and DG, Border Guard Bangladesh have signed an agreement, to review all pending works in such a way that Indian villages which are situated fully or partially outside the existing fence will come entirely inside the fencing.<br/><br/><br/><br/>  <br/>                           **********

records.qtitle: New avenues under Make in India programme
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether ''Make in India'' programme is likely to create an environment of trust to convince industry leaders of Government''s commitment to developing the industry;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether the country has slipped low in the list of countries in terms of ‘ease of doing business’ across the world;<br/><br/>(d) 	if so, whether the ''Make in India'' campaign will open new avenues of doing business; and<br/><br/>(e) 	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY<br/>(SHRI C.R. CHAUDHARY)<br/><br/>(a) & (b): 	‘Make in India’ initiative was launched on 25th September, 2014 with the objective of facilitating investment, fostering innovation, building best in class manufacturing infrastructure, making it easy to do business and enhancing skill development. Action Plans for 21 key sectors were identified for specific action in the following areas:-<br/><br/>(i) Policy Initiatives (ii) Fiscal incentives (iii) Infrastructure Creation (iv) Ease of Doing Business (v) Innovation and R&D (vi) Skill Development.<br/><br/>Further, Government of India, under its ‘Ease of Doing Business’ initiative, aims at creating a conducive environment by streamlining the existing regulations and processes and eliminating unnecessary requirements and procedures. A detailed plan of regulatory reforms has been implemented not only in the Central Government Ministries but also in States and Union Territories through the active involvement of State Governments & UT administrations.<br/><br/>(c) to (e): 	No, Sir. India’s rank has rather improved by 30 positions to 100 in the last Doing Business Report of the World Bank released on 31st October, 2017. <br/><br/>By facilitating investments, building a conducive environment for innovation, improving infrastructure, skilling the youth of the country and by easing the regulatory environment, the Make in India campaign will open new avenues of doing business.<br/><br/>******* <br/>

records.qtitle: Embezzlement of funds in Banks
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) the steps taken against Banks/officials who were involved in carrying out irregular transactions and violating the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) instructions, creating mismanagement in Banks after demonetisation, the details thereof, Bank-wise including Private Sector Banks; and<br/><br/>(b) the steps taken or being taken by Government to avoid recurrence of incidents of embezzlement of funds of banks and similar types of instances in future and strengthening of the banking system?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b): Public Sector Banks (PSBs) have reported that as on 01.05.2017, based on the irregularities noticed during demonetisation, they had placed 209 officials under suspension and transferred 132 officials. Wherever considered appropriate, Banks have lodged complaints with Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)/Police.<br/><br/>Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had advised the banks vide circular dated November 29, 2016 to take action to prevent / detect / contain the malpractices or wrongdoing by staff in branches engaged in exchange / deposit of Specified Bank Notes (SBNs). In the said circular, banks were also advised to strengthen the internal / concurrent audit process in the bank including random visits / scrutinies so as to detect and avoid any malpractice in the exchange / deposit of SBNs in the branches. <br/><br/>Further vide RBI DBS circular Ref. No.DBS.CO.PPD / 4480/11.01.005/2016-17 dated December 8, 2016 banks were advised to track the complete trail of cash movements in large quantities so as to ensure that the extant instructions of RBI are followed both in letter and spirit. Further a list of 22 action points (illustrative) was also forwarded to banks with advice to utilise their internal audit resources to monitor the position and bring any anomalies noticed to their Audit Committee of the Board so as to ensure that necessary action is taken in all such cases, apart from reporting the summary of findings to RBI.<br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Inclusion of foreign airlines and pilots in Regional Connectivity Scheme
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) whether there are enough specialised aircrafts to carry out operations for Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) from the identified airports, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b) whether pilots are being included to carry out training to implement the regional connectivity scheme for the present identified airports, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) whether foreign airlines and pilot personnel would be included in the process for the regional connectivity scheme and if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Jayant Sinha)<br/><br/>(a):It is a market driven scheme and operators bid for the route and airport combinations on the basis of their business plan.  It is the operator, who has to decide on the type and make of aircraft depending on the routes selected / awarded. <br/><br/>(b):RCS (UDAN) does not entail any specialized training for RCS airports.  It is normal operational matter dealt by respective Selected Airline Operator.  <br/><br/>(c): As per eligibility criteria in the scheme, a valid air operator permit or equivalent permit issued by the competent civil aviation regulatory authority of any foreign country is eligible to submit the proposal under RCS (UDAN).<br/>As per para 3.2.1.5 of the Scheme "DGCA may also examine, from time to time, permitting operations under the Scheme using foreign registered aircraft and may issue appropriate guidelines / directions in this regard."<br/>

records.qtitle: Modernisation of weather forecasting technology
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: <br/>(a)	whether outdated technology, old equipments and shortage of skilled staff are causing hurdles for the India Meteorological Department (IMD) in weather prediction;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor;<br/>(c)	whether the Government proposes to purchase latest equipment, increase staff, upgrade/modernize the technology in weather centres and if so, the details thereof;<br/>(d)	the details of funds required and allocated for the purpose; and<br/>(e)	the other steps taken/being taken to enhance the capability and improve functioning of IMD?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER FOR MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY <br/>AND MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES<br/>(DR. HARSH VARDHAN)<br/><br/>(a)-(b)  No Sir.<br/><br/>(c)	Augmentation of observational systems is a continuing process. IMD also has a program for the upgradation of (i) advanced data assimilation tools (ii) advanced communication and IT infrastructure (iv) high performance computing systems and (v) intensive/sophisticated training of IMD personnel to facilitate the implementation of advanced global/regional/ meso-scale prediction models for improving the accuracy of weather forecasts in all temporal and spatial scales and for quick dissemination of weather forecast assessments/warnings to the users.<br/>		<br/>A High Performance Computing System with 6.8 Petaflop speed has been commissioned to meet the modelling requirements. This system is now the fastest super computing system in the country. <br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>Under the Scheme “Integrated Himalayan Meteorology Programme for Western & Central Himalayas”(IHMP), ten (10) Nos. of X Band Doppler Weather Radars are proposed to be installed during 2017-2020 at the stations in three States;  J&K, H.P. and Uttarakhand for improving the observing systems for severe weather services.<br/><br/>Under Gramin Krishi Mausam Sewa (GKMS), District Agro-Met Units (DAMUs) will be established at Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) in each district in collaboration with ICAR to implement district level Agromet Advisory Services during 2017-20.  In addition to existing 130 Agromet Field Units (AMFUs) which will act as DAMUs for the districts of their location, 530 DAMUs will be established in a phased wise manner. The network of DAMUs will be extended to cover all the districts by March 2020.<br/><br/> (d)     The funds are allocated scheme-wise.  The following schemes have been approved by Govt. of India for implementation during 2017-20:-<br/><br/>Sl No.	Name of the Scheme/Project	Budget Outlays (Rs. in Crores)<br/>1	Weather & Climate Services	450.00<br/>2	Commissioning of Polarimetric Doppler Weather Radar (DWRs) 	99.20<br/>3	Upgradation of Forecast System	310.40<br/>4	Atmospheric Observations Network	439.60<br/><br/>(e)	Further upgradation of the weather forecasting capabilities is underway through implementation of  the following programs (i) Atmospheric Observations Network, (ii) Upgradation of Forecast System, (iii) Weather & Climate Services and (iv) Commissioning of Polarimetric Doppler Weather Radars during 2017-20 and beyond.

records.qtitle: Implementation of indigenous technology
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has taken steps to implement various indigenous technologies that have been developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) during the last three years;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to engage start-ups in various initiatives and innovations related to defence sector?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>SHRIMATI NIRMALA SITHARAMAN<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b):  Yes Sir. A new provision has been stipulated at Para 72, Chapter-II of Defence Procurement Policy (DPP-2016), for production of system developed by DRDO through Indian industry. List of systems developed by DRDO and approved for induction in the last three years is placed at Appendix ‘A’.<br/><br/>(c)  In pursuance of the Defence Production Policy, Ministry of Defence, Government of India has set up a new scheme Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme under ‘Make in India’ initiative, which aims at funding the development of defence and dual use technologies that are currently not available with the Indian defence industry or have not been developed so far. <br/><br/>     		The funding will be through provision of grants to public and private sector industry especially MSMEs to carry out innovation, research and development. The focus will be on funding for the development of technologies that will form the kernel of components/ Assemblies, which will in turn be used to develop the defence equipments/systems/sub-systems/platforms.<br/><br/>     		The cost of development spread across all the required technology development phases is up to INR 10 Crore through this scheme and typically projects will not exceed a development period of two years.<br/><br/>     		TDF scheme has been implemented and executed by DRDO. More than 600 Industries have been registered on a web-portal reflecting the industries keen interest in Technology Development Fund Scheme.<br/><br/>      	In the first round, three projects have been awarded.   Further sanctioning of projects is    a continuous process.<br/><br/>Further, in the recently promulgated procedure for ‘Make-II’ sub-category of ‘Make’ procedure, eligibility criteria for participation by Start-ups in ‘Make-II’ process has been relaxed.<br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Direct trains connecting Ranchi to Ahmedabad  Surat
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) the number of direct trains connecting Ranchi in Jharkhand to Ahmedabad/Surat in Gujarat;<br/><br/>(b) whether the Ministry has received any proposal/representation since long to start direct trains between Ranchi and Ahmedabad/Surat;<br/><br/>(c) if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(d) whether Railways carried out any survey to check potential to start a new train between these stations; and<br/><br/>(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI RAJEN GOHAIN)<br/><br/>(a)  At present, one pair of weekly service viz. 13425/13426 Malda Town-Surat Express (weekly) provides direct connection between Ranchi and Surat.  However, no direct train is presently available between Ranchi and Ahmedabad.  <br/><br/>(b) & (c) Yes, Sir.  Request for introduction of a train between Ranchi and Ahmedabad/Surat has been received inter alia from Member of Legislative Assembly of Jharkhand and Members of ZRUCC. Similar request for introduction of a train from Ranchi to Gujarat has also been received from one Hon’ble Member of Parliament<br/><br/>(d) & (e) On Indian Railways, the occupancy of existing trains is monitored on a regular basis to assess the traffic pattern. Accordingly, the occupancy of train No. 13425/13426 Malda Town-Surat Express during period from April 2017 to February 2018 has been analysed and it has been found that the same was more than 100%. On sectors not connected by trains, such analysis is not feasible.  Moreover, due to operational constraints, at present, introduction of train between Ranchi and Ahmedabad/Surat is not feasible.  <br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Licence to CSCs for functioning as payment gateways
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: -<br/><br/>(a)	whether the Common Service Centres (CSCs) have been allotted license for functioning as payment gateways;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c)	the number of CSCs opened in villages and rural districts alongwith the number of employment opportunities created so far; and<br/><br/>(d)	the details of achievement of CSC in creating a cashless society? <br/><br/>
records.ans_text: (a) and (b):	No, Sir.  CSC  has not been allotted licence  to work  as payment gateways.<br/><br/>(c):	Till February, 2018, there are 1,83,184 Common Services Centres (CSCs) functioning at Gram Panchayat (GP) level across the country.<br/>	<br/>One CSC on an average provides employment to 3 - 4 persons.<br/>(d):	The Government of India launched the Digital Finance Inclusion, Awareness & Access (DFIAA) Project under Digital India programme in November, 2016 to March, 2017.  CSC Special Purpose Vehicle (CSC-SPV) has implemented this project through CSC- Digital Seva Kendras and registered more than 205 lakh Citizens and enabled around 26 lakh merchants during the period November, 2016 to March, 2017.<br/><br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Disbursal of stipend to research students
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government is aware that there is delay in disbursing stipend by University Grants Commission (UGC) for research students even after qualifying Junior Research Fellowship (JRF)/National Eligibility Test (NET);<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) whether Government has effected any budgetary cut for research in higher education; and<br/><br/>(d) if so, the details thereof ?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(Dr. SATYA PAL SINGH)<br/><br/>(a)	& (b): No Sir. The University Grants Commission (UGC) has informed that there is no reported delay in disbursing stipend by UGC for research students during financial year 2017-18. However, in a few cases, delay might have occurred in the disbursements of stipend amounts to research students due to the following factors:<br/>i)	late joining by candidates; <br/>ii)	delay in uploading of Master Data by Institutions; <br/>iii)	Technical problem in PFMS<br/><br/>The UGC scholarships are now disbursed to beneficiaries through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and Public Financial Management System (PFMS) to ensure quick, hasslefree and timely payment of scholarship dues. Further, the UGC periodical reviews and monitors timely disbursement of scholarships to the intended beneficiaries.<br/>(c): No, Sir. UGC has informed that there is no budgetary cut for research in Higher Education.<br/>(d): Does not arise.<br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Beneficiaries of housing schemes
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: <br/>(a) whether the provisions have been made in the housing scheme by Government for those eligible beneficiaries who have not been included in the list of 2011;<br/>(b) if so, the number of such beneficiaries, State-wise; <br/>(c) if not, the steps likely to be taken by Government in this regard; and <br/>(d) whether Government proposes to formulate any scheme for this purpose and if so, the details thereof?<br/> <br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN AFFAIRS<br/><br/>              [SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI]<br/> <br/>(a) to (d):	 Yes, Sir.  The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) [PMAY(U)] to achieve the Government’s vision of “Housing for All by 2022”.   The Mission provides financial assistance to all States/UTs in addressing the housing requirements of urban poor including the slum dwellers, who do not own pucca house anywhere in the country, through following four verticals:<br/>(i)	“In-situ” Slum Redevelopment (ISSR);	 <br/>(ii)	Credit-Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS;	<br/>(iii)	Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP); and	<br/>(iv)	Beneficiary-led individual house construction or enhancement (BLC).<br/><br/>All urban poor including slum dwellers belonging to Economic Weaker Section (EWS) and people belonging to Lower Income Group (LIG), Middle Income Group (MIG) categories in urban area, irrespective of their inclusion in the list of 2011, are eligible under the PMAY(U). <br/><br/>All the Statutory towns across the country as per Census 2011 and towns notified subsequently including notified Planning/Development area are eligible for coverage under the PMAY(U).<br/><br/>Under the PMAY (U), States/ UTs undertake demand survey for assessing actual demand of housing.  Based on the assessed demand for housing, the States/ UTs frame the project proposals and after approval from the concerned State Level Sanctioning & Monitoring Committee (SLSMC) they submit the proposals to the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs for central assistance. <br/>State-wise details of house sanctioned for the eligible beneficiaries under the PMAY(U) is at Annexure. <br/><br/>                           ******<br/>

records.qtitle: Salient features of NCS and MCC Schemes
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	the details and salient features of the National Career Service (NCS) Scheme and Model Career Centre (MCC) Scheme;<br/><br/>(b)	whether Government has received proposals from various State Governments for setting up Model Career Centres in their respective States;<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof and the action taken by Government thereon along with the funds allocated and utilized for the purpose during each of the last three years and the current year, State/UT-wise; and<br/><br/>(d)	the manner and extent to which NCS and MCC have benefited the job seekers in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (IC) FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>(SHRI SANTOSH GANGWAR)<br/><br/>(a): The National Career Service provides a variety of employment related services like job matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information on skill development courses, apprenticeship, internships, online at NCS portal (www.ncs.gov.in) accessible from multiple delivery channels.<br/><br/><br/>The NCS Portal is supported by multi-lingual Call Centre/ Helpdesk to assist and guide jobseekers in accessing the employment related services. The NCS portal also has a repository of career content for access by all and a network of Career Counselors. Government has engaged several institutions and organisations to bring more and more job opportunities.<br/><br/>The NCS Project envisages setting up of 100 Model Career Centres (MCCs) to be established in collaboration with States and institutions of repute to provide variety of employment related services using technology.The Model Career Centre function under the administrative control of the State Governments.The NCS Project has also been enhanced to interlink the employment exchanges with NCS Portal and central funding for up gradation of employment exchanges in the country and for organising job fairs by State Government.<br/><br/>(b) to (c): Yes, Sir. The Government has considered the proposals submitted by the state Government for financial assistance for setting up of Model Career Centres. The State/UTs wise details regarding allocated and utilized funds of these centres are at Annex -I.<br/><br/>(d): NCS and MCC are the linking point between jobseekers and employers to get digitise online employment related solutions. The NCS has over 4.21 core job seekers and 14.87 Lakh employers registered on the Portal and mobilized 8.43 Lakh vacancies till date. Under NCS 1374 job fairs have been conducted in which around 1.84 Lakh job seekers have been selected for various jobs.<br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR CULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE FOR ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE<br/><br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) National Artistes Welfare Fund and Artistes Pension Scheme and Welfare Fund were ingredients of a single Scheme titled “Artistes Pension Scheme and Welfare” being administered by Ministry of Culture. <br/><br/>Subsequent to review of the Scheme beyond 12th Five Year Plan in 2017 the nomenclature of the Scheme has been modified as “Scheme for Pension and Medical Aid to Artistes”. The purpose of the scheme is to improve financial and socio-economic status of the old artistes and scholars who have contributed significantly in their specialized fields of arts, letters etc. in their active age or are still contributing in the field of arts, letters etc. but due to old age they have to lead a miserable life or are in penury condition.  Under the scheme, financial assistance from the Government is provided in the form of monthly allowance to the artistes recommended under the Centre-State Quota on sharing basis, with the latter paying a monthly allowance of at least Rs.500/- per month per beneficiary. The monthly allowance contributed by the Central Government in such cases shall not exceed Rs.3500/- per month per beneficiary.  In any circumstances the contribution of Central Government and State Government/UT Administration altogether will not exceed Rs.4000/- per month per beneficiary.  The Scheme has also provision to provide medical aid facility to these Artistes and his/her spouse by covering them under a convenient and affordable health insurance scheme of the Government. <br/><br/>The details of funds allocated, released and spent under the erstwhile ‘Artistes Pension Scheme and Welfare Fund’ during the last three years are as under:<br/><br/>(Rs. records.qtitle: Steps to reduce cost of production and import of coal
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	whether adequate steps have been taken to reduce production cost and also import of coal and if so, the details thereof;  <br/>(b)	whether steps have also been taken for rationalization of coal linkages and if so, the details thereof; and  <br/>(c)	to what extent these steps have been successful?  <br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND COAL <br/>(SHRI PIYUSH GOYAL)<br/><br/>(a): Some of the measures taken to bring down the cost of productionby Coal India Limited (CIL) include the following:<br/>(i)	e-reverse auction for finalization of contracts for explosives implemented.<br/>(ii)	Action taken for improving competition in tenders and cost reduction:<br/> <br/>a)	In case of procurement, introduction of Reverse Auction (RA) for tenders valued more than 1 crore with Start Bid price as L1-bid<br/>b)	Introduction of rejection of H-1 bid in RA to generate competition and obtain more realistic "Start Bid Price" <br/>c)	Non-disclosure of Bidder''s identity in RA.<br/><br/>(iii)	Staggering the day of rest so that the infrastructure is utilized for higher number of days without affecting the period of rest for an individual. <br/><br/>(iv)	Adoption of mechanization in both underground and opencast mines.<br/><br/>(v)	Converting unsafe, unviable underground mines into opencast mines.<br/><br/>(vi)	Higher size HEMM to be deployed in major open cast projects for maximum extraction of coal economically.<br/><br/>As per the current import policy, coal is kept under Open General License (OGL) and consumers are free to import coal from the source of their choice as per their contractual prices on payment of applicable duty. However, to reduce import of coal, CIL had taken steps for promotion of import substitution through source rationalization with part supply from higher grade coal sources.  More coal from various sources including higher grade were offered through various types of e- auction schemes particularly special forward e-auction with flexi lifting to cater the requirement of various power sector consumers not having FSA with CIL sources. However, the gap between demand and supply of coal cannot be bridged completely as there is insufficient domestic availability of coking coal and power plants designed on imported coal will continue to import coal for their production.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>(b) to (c): An Inter-Ministerial Task Force was constituted in June, 2014 for review of existing coal sources as also feasibility for rationalization of these sources with a view to optimize transportation cost. Coal Linkage rationalization in Power sector has resulted in decrease in transportation cost of coal from the mines to the power plants leading to more efficient coal based generation of Power. Total coal movement rationalization of 54.76 MT has taken place with annual potential savings of Rs. 3354 Crore.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Demands and supply of fertilizers
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a)	whether there is a considerable time lag between indented demand and 	actual supply of fertilizers and if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b) 	the quantum of fertilizers demanded and supplied to the States during the 	last three years and projected for the current year, State-wise; <br/><br/>(c) 	whether the quantity of fertilizers supplied is not adequate to meet the 	requirement of the States and if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(d)	 the remedial steps being taken by the Government in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS<br/><br/><br/>                                       (RAO INDERJIT SINGH)<br/>____________________________________________________________(a)  : 	Department of Agriculture Cooperation & Farmers Welfare (DAC&FW) in consultation with States/ UTs assesses the requirement of all subsidised fertilizers before the start of each Season. Department of Fertilizers ensures availability of fertilizers at the State level and the distribution to the farmers within the State is the responsibility of the respective State Government. Availability of all fertilizers in the country has been adequate and there is no report of delay in supply from any State.<br/> <br/>(b) & (c): Two statements indicating the quantum of fertilizers demanded and supplied to the States during the last three years and projected for the current year, State-wise are placed at Annexure ‘A’ and Annexure ‘B’ respectively. It can be seen from the statements that there is no shortage of any fertilizers as availability was more than the sales. <br/><br/>(d):     In view of (b) & (c) above, question does not rise.<br/><br/><br/>                    ********<br/>

records.qtitle: Proposals for One Stop Centres

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. VIRENDRA KUMAR)<br/><br/>(a):     The Ministry is implementing scheme for setting up One Stop Centre since 1st April 2015 to support women affected by violence. records.qtitle: Increase in funds for education to STs girls

records.qtitle: Use of Wi fi in commercial aircrafts
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)  whether  Government  proposes  to allow  the  use  of  Wi-Fi  in  commercial aircrafts operating over Indian Territory;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government has carried out a study to examine the security implications of the same; and<br/><br/>(c)  whether  the  Directorate  General  of Civil  Aviation  (DGCA)  has  issued  any direction  to  restrict  the  carrying  of  certain mobile  phones  in  the  flights  in  view  of reported incidents of accidents in the flights?<br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Jayant Sinha)<br/><br/>(a): The proposal for providing on-board Wi-Fi services involves amendment of provisions of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 and Indian Telegraph Rules made thereunder.
