records.qtitle: Job opportunities for tribal girls in Jharkhand
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: 3214.     SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI: <br/><br/>Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether job opportunities for tribal girls are not enough to protect them from exploitation;<br/>(b) if so, the details of specific steps taken by Government to increase job opportunities for tribal girls especially in Jharkhand; and<br/>(c) the details of the measures taken to create job opportunities in the most backward districts of Jharkhand?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>        (SHRI MALLIKARJUN KHARGE)<br/>	<br/>(a) Government of India is implementing various employment generation and poverty alleviation programmes in both rural and urban areas to increase employment opportunities, such as, Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA); Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY); Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY); and Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP). The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing a programme titled “Special Central Assistance to Tribal Sub-Plan (SCA to TSP) for employment-cum-income generation activities of BPL Scheduled Tribes. The ultimate objective of this programme is to boost the demand-based income-generation and thus raise the economic and social status of tribals. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs supplements the efforts of other Ministries like Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Labour and Employment, etc. in economic upliftment of the tribals in the country.<br/><br/>(b) & (c) The Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the following schemes in the country including Jharkhand for the education and self employment of STs:- <br/><br/>(i) Scheme of Strengthening Education among Scheduled Tribe (ST) Girls in Low Literacy Districts. <br/>(ii) Scheme of construction of hostels for ST Girls and Boys. <br/>(iii) Scheme of Establishment of Ashram Schools in Tribal Sub Plan Areas. <br/>(iv) Vocational Training in Tribal Areas. <br/>(v) Post-Matric Scholarship for ST students. <br/>(vi) Upgradation of Merit of ST students. <br/>(vii) Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for STs. <br/>(viii) Scheme of National Overseas Scholarship for STs. <br/>(ix) Top Class Education for ST student.<br/>(x) Grants-in-aid to Voluntary Organizations (under which residential, non- residential schools, computer training centres and knitting, weaving & handloom training centres run by NGOs for ST students are supported, apart from hospitals, mobile dispensaries etc.).<br/><br/>Apart from above schemes, Ministry of Tribal Affairs also administers grant under Article 275 (1) under which grant is also used for setting up of “Eklavaya Model Residential Schools” for providing quality education to ST students (both girls and boys) from class VI to XII.  National Scheduled Tribes Financial and Development Corporation provides financial assistance for setting up Project costing upto Rs. 10 lakh per unit.<br/>……<br/>

records.qtitle: Naxal affected States
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) the details of the States suffering badly by the Naxal problem;<br/><br/>(b) the State-wise number of people including tribals and security personnel<br/>killed in various naxal attacks during last three years;<br/><br/>(c) whether there is a proper co-ordination between State police and para- military forces in these States to effectively tackle the Naxal menace;<br/><br/>(d) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(e) the steps taken  to modernize the State police force and intelligence agencies to strengthen them?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI  JITENDRA SINGH)<br/><br/>(a):	Nine states, namely, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal are considered Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected states.<br/><br/>(b):	The number of security forces and civilians killed in various naxal attacks during last three years, state-wise, are annexed.  The number of tribals killed, is not maintained separately by this Ministry.  However, a large number of persons killed by the LWE under the ‘civilians’ category include Adivasis.<br/><br/>(c) & (d):	There is proper coordination between the State Police Forces and Central Armed Police Forces in carrying out anti-naxal operations.  In order to ensure better coordination, meetings between State Police Forces and Central Armed Police Forces are held regularly at the district level and the state level.  The Ministry of Home Affairs also regularly holds coordination meetings of Directors General of Police of the States and Directors General of the Central Armed Police Forces.<br/><br/>(e):	In order to modernize the State Police forces, the Government of India provides funds under the scheme of Modernization of State Police Forces (MPF).  In addition, the Government is also providing financial assistance under various schemes like the Security Related Expenditure (SRE), the Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) and Construction/ Strengthening of Fortified Police Stations.  With a view to strengthen the security apparatus, the Central Government has provided financial assistance to states to raise India Reserve Battalions.  To provide training to state forces to effectively combat LWE, the Central Government has provided assistance to set up 15 Counter Insurgency and Anti-Terrorist (CIAT) Schools in LWE affected States.  Several steps have been taken to strengthen and upgrade the capabilities of intelligence agencies at the Central and State level.  This includes intelligence sharing through Multi-Agency Centre (MAC) at the central level and State Multi Agency Centre (SMAC) at the state level.<br/><br/>                                 *******<br/>

records.qtitle: Increasing incidence of non  communicable diseases
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) whether an increasing incidence of non-communicable diseases is seen in the country;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and factors responsible for this state of affairs; and<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to meet the situation?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER FOR HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)<br/><br/>(a) & (b): Yes. The exact number of peoples suffering from various non-communicable diseases is not known. However based on the Report of the National Commission on Macroeconomics and Health, estimated number of cases of important non-communicable diseases are given below: <br/>•	Cardiovascular Diseases: 3.80 crore in 2005; Projected increase is 6.41 crore in 2015 <br/><br/>•	Diabetes: 3.10 crore in 2005; Projected increase is 4.60 crore in 2015 <br/><br/>•	Stroke: 12 lakh in 2005; Projected increase is 17 lakh in 2015 <br/><br/>The exact reasons for high prevalence of NCDs are not clear.  However, urbanisation and longevity has been associated with increase in NCDs. Unhealthy lifestyle is major reason for increase in NCDs. The four major risk factors which are directly or indirectly associated with the causation of chronic non-communicable disease are as follows:-<br/><br/>(i)  Tobacco use (smoking & chewing)<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>(ii)  Alcohol use<br/>(iii) Physical inactivity<br/>(iv)  Unhealthy diet.<br/><br/>(c) To control the NCDs in India, Government of India has initiated the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS) in the 100 identified Districts in 21 States.  <br/><br/>.........<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Targeted Fiscal Deficit
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: <br/>(a)	the Centre’s Fiscal Deficit during  the first half of 2011-12 i.e. April-  September,2011 as per cent of targeted deficit for the whole year;     <br/><br/>(b)	how is compares with the same period last year i.e. 2010-11;   <br/><br/>(c)	reasons for increased deficit this year as compared to last year; and <br/>	<br/>(d)	the details of efforts made by Government to mobile resources to ease the pressure?<br/><br/> <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>                         <br/>                     (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA) <br/><br/> <br/>(a) 	For the period upto September,2011, the fiscal deficit is Rs.2,80,810 crore which is 68 per cent of the Budget Estimates of 2011-12;   <br/>(b)	The fiscal deficit upto September,2010 was Rs.1,33,252 crore which was 34.9 per cent of Budget Estimates of 2010 -11;<br/><br/>(c)	Increase in fiscal deficit during the first half of 2011-12 is due to front    loading of direct tax refunds in the current year.  Lower fiscal deficit during the first half of 2010-11 was on account of  one time receipt of non-tax revenue from auction of 3G & BWA spectrum;<br/><br/>(d)	To contain the fiscal deficit in 2011-12, Government has advised all Ministries/Departments to adhere to the expenditure ceilings in the Budget Estimates 2011-12. They have also advised to meet additional expenditure requirements, if any, during the year through savings from the overall expenditure outlays.  Instructions have also been issued to concerned Departments to make concerted efforts to achieve the revenue collection targets for 2011-12.     <br/>                       ***<br/>

records.qtitle: Benefits of AIBP
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the benefits of Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP) have reached 	in the remote rural areas, tribal areas, etc.; <br/>(b) 	if so, the benefits that the rural people especially women and tribals are accruing from 	AIBP;<br/>(c) 	whether this programme has been reviewed by Government; and<br/>(d) 	if so, the outcome of this review? <br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES & MINORITY AFFAIRS ( SHRI VINCENT H. PALA) <br/><br/>(a) & (b) 	Irrigation being a state subject, the irrigation projects are planned, executed, funded by State Governments from their own resources and as per their priorities. The Union Government provides Central Assistance (CA) under Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) to the States as per guidelines for completion of ongoing projects.  Preferential funding to extent of 90% of the project cost is provided under AIBP to the projects benefiting Drought Prone Area (DPAP),  tribal areas and projects in special category states. The Special Category States covers the North Eastern States, Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Uttaranchal.  The projects in the undivided Koraput, Bolangir and Kalahandi (KBK) districts of Orissa also treated at par with Special Category States. As such, benefits under AIBP are provided to remote, rural areas and tribal areas. <br/><br/>(c) & (d) 	The guidelines for AIBP funding are being revised from time to time in order to enhance the scope of funding as well as to allow special consideration for the regions lagging behind in development, which presently include north-eastern states, hilly states, drought prone and tribal areas, KBK districts of Orissa, states with lower irrigation development as compared to national average and districts identified under PM package for agrarian distressed districts.<br/><br/>****<br/>

records.qtitle: (clubbed) Integrated water management
records.name: BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the Planning Commission has formulated any policy regarding integrated water 	management to remove the water crisis in the country;<br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c) 	whether the Commission has submitted the said policy documents;<br/>(d) 	if so, by when the policy is likely to be implemented; and<br/>(e) 	how Jharkhand would be benefited in this policy?	<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES & MINORITY AFFAIRS ( SHRI VINCENT H. PALA) <br/><br/>		(a) to (d)   Planning Commission has informed that during the 55th meeting of National 	Development Council (NDC) held on 24.7.2010, it was decided that “The Planning Commission 	would prepare an integrated policy for water resources management that would be discussed in 	the future NDC meeting”. In pursuance of the above decision Member (WR), Planning 	Commission made a presentation to the Prime minister on 6.4.11 and after the meeting it was 	decided that:<br/>(i)	Ministry of Water Resources in consultation with the Planning Commission should prepare a comprehensive document on water related issues for consideration of NDC.<br/>(ii)	Development of State specific action plans in consultation with the States on the lines indicated in the meeting.<br/>	On the decisions (i) and (ii) above, Planning Commission has constituted eight Working 	Groups and one Steering Committee chaired by Member (WR), Planning Commission for the 	formulation of the Twelfth Five Year Plan to address the issues involved in water management.<br/>		(e) 		The above applies to entire country including Jharkhand.<br/>****<br/>

records.qtitle: Performance of IID Centres in  Jharkhand
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: 2855.		SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a)	the total number of Integrated Infrastructure Development (IID) Centres functioning in the country, State-wise;<br/>(b)	what has been performance of these IID Centres, especially in Jharkhand; <br/>(c)	how these have been successful in achieving the objectives for which they have been set up;<br/>(d)	whether Government proposes to set up more IID Centres in the country;<br/>(e)	if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(f)	the details of package/assistance provided to various States including Jharkhand to strengthen the small scale sector and enhance its competitiveness in the national and international markets? <br/>
records.ans_text: (a):	102 Infrastructure Development (ID) Centres (77 New and 25 upgradation) are functioning in the country, supported under Micro and Small Enterprises – Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP). Details are given at Annexure-I. <br/><br/>(b):	10739 plots have been allotted in new ID Centres.  Details are given at Annexure-I. <br/> <br/>(c):	3819 units have been set up in new ID Centres.  Details are given at Annexure-I. <br/><br/>(d):	Yes, Sir. <br/><br/>(e):	29 ID Centres are under various stages of implementation. Details are given at Annexure-II<br/> <br/>(f):	The Government is implementing various schemes / programmes for promotion and development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) for all the states including Jharkhand. The major schemes include Credit Guarantee Scheme, Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme, Performance and Credit Rating Scheme, Cluster Development Programme, National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme and Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme.  In addition, Government announced “Package on Promotion of Micro and Small Enterprises” on 27.2.07, which, inter-alia, provide for legislation, credit support, fiscal support, support for cluster based development, technology and quality upgradation, marketing, entrepreneurial and managerial development and strengthening of data base for MSME Sector.  <br/>

records.qtitle: Surprise checks to ensure cleanliness and passenger amenities
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)  	whether standard of cleanliness in railway coaches as well as on platform has gone down considerably in recent years;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details of measures taken by Railways to ensure cleanliness and better passenger amenities in coaches and on platforms for passengers;<br/><br/>(c)	whether any surprise checks are being carried out to ensure proper upkeep of coaches and railway stations; and<br/><br/>(d)	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI BHARATSINH SOLANKI)<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b)  	No, Sir. Indian Railways always endeavour to improve upon the standards of cleanliness and hygiene in coaches and stations. <br/><br/>For further improving upon the standards of cleanliness in coaches, schemes like Intensive mechanized cleaning, On Board House-Keeping Services (OBHS) and cleaning attention to trains during their stoppage at “Clean Train Stations” etc. have also been launched. Indian Railways have also planned multi-pronged action by synergizing technology, education of users and provision of better mechanized equipments to improve upon the standards of cleanliness at stations. <br/><br/>(c) & (d)	Regular Inspections/Checks are carried out at various levels to monitor the standard of cleanliness and upkeep of coaches and stations and punitive action is taken wherever warranted. Besides, special drives are also launched from time to time to intensify the level of cleanliness in coaches and stations and corrective action is taken wherever deficiency is noticed.<br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Crash of BSF helicopter in Jharkhand
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) whether a Border Security Force (BSF) helicopter crashed in Jharkhand<br/>recently;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) whether the helicopter was on an anti-naxalite operation;<br/><br/>(d) whether it was a sabotage or whether naxalite forces were behind the crash, directly or indirectly; and<br/><br/>(e) what precautionary steps have been taken to avoid such crashes in future?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI JITENDRA SINGH) <br/><br/>(a): Yes Sir.  BSF’s ALH/Dhruv VT-BSH helicopter crashed on 19.10.2011 in the State of Jharkhand.<br/><br/>(b): The helicopter VT-BSH was serviceable and operating at Ranchi airbase.  On 19 Oct 2011, it took of at 0839 hrs and after 10 minutes, it met with a fatal accident in between village Kolad and Remta, Police Station Namkum, Dist-Ranchi while enroute to Chaibasa from Ranchi airbase.<br/><br/><br/>The following persons of M/s Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd. (PHHL) died in the accident:-<br/>(i)	Capt S P Singh, Pilot<br/>(ii)	Capt K V Thomas, Co-Pilot<br/>(iii)	Mr Manoj Kumar Swain, Technician<br/><br/>(c): No Sir. The said assignment was in connection with the visit of officials of Ministry of Rural Development to naxal affected areas.<br/><br/>(d): The investigation by Ministry of Civil Aviation/Directorate General Civil Aviation is in progress.<br/><br/>(e): It is ensured that all the safety measures such as fire fighting equipment, medical & security cover, and wind socks/smoke candle are available at the helipads/airstrips.  Trial landing are also done prior to actual flying operaton wherever required.  Before carrying out any flying commitment in LWE areas, the helipads are secured and sanitized.  Safety, operation & maintenance audit of all bases is done by team of BSF, Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd. and Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd.<br/><br/>*******<br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Import of plastic wastes
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: <br/>a)	whether the country imports plastic wastes;<br/><br/>b)	if so, for what purpose and give details of quantities, costs and countries from which the plastic wastes were imported during the last three years; and<br/><br/>c)	whether there is any proposal to reprocess/recycle plastic in the Special Economic Zones (SEZs), if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY<br/>(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA)<br/><br/>(a)	to (c): Our Foreign Trade Policy permits import of plastic waste. Imports take place to bridge the gap between demand and supply of the item. The import of waste of PET bottles is free. Import of other plastic wastes/ scrap is restricted and allowed against authorization. Plastic reprocessing / recycling units are allowed to be set up in the Special Economic Zones (SEZs). The details of the imports in terms of quantities, values and countries of imports are available in the  DGCI&S publication in CD form namely ‘Monthly Statistics of Foreign Trade of India’ Volume-II, which is regularly sent to Parliament library by DGCI&S.<br/>                                                                    <br/><br/>                                                                      ************<br/>

records.qtitle: Healthcare services in remote rural areas
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: GOVERNMENT OF INDIA<br/>MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/><br/> RAJYA  SABHA<br/>UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2261<br/>TO BE ANSWERED ON 13TH  DECEMBER, 2011<br/>HEALTHCARE SERVICES IN REMOTE RURAL AREAS<br/><br/>2261. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) the manner in which Government proposes to meet the challenges of<br/>providing quality health services in remote rural areas as well as tribal and hilly areas in the country; and<br/><br/>(b) the current status for provision of quality health services in the tribal areas of<br/>Jharkhand?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI SUDIP BANDYOPADHYAY)<br/><br/>(a)& (b) National Rural Health Mission was launched in the year 2005 with an aim to provide accessible, affordable and quality healthcare to the rural population of the country including remote rural areas as well as tribal and hilly areas. The Government has taken several steps to meet the challenges in providing quality healthcare  across the country including the State of Jharkhand which include the following:<br/><br/>1.	Financial Assistance has been provided to the States for augmentation of health human resources through contractual appointments of doctors, specialists nurses, paramedics etc. In the State of Jharkhand, 528 doctors including AYUSH doctors, 31 specialists, 862 Staff Nurses, 4098 ANMs and 576 parameidcs have been engaged under NRHM to provide healthcare services.<br/><br/>2.	 For improving the skills of Doctors and paramedics and to enable improved skilled care at birth, States are encouraged to conduct various training programmes such as Skilled Birth Attendant(SBA), Life Saving Anesthesia Skills (LSAS), Basic Emergency and Obstetrics Care(BeMOC), Emergency Obstetrics Care(EmOC),   etc . <br/> <br/>3.	Funds have been provided to the States including to the State of Jhrakhand for infrastructure upgradation /renovation of health care <br/><br/><br/>facilities as per standards. So far, under NRHM, new constriction works of 182 health facilities (PHCs, CHCs, Sub-Centre) and renovation/upgrdation of 3 District Hospitals have been undertaken in Jharkhand.<br/><br/>4.	States are encouraged to setup Sick New Born Care Units (SNCU) at District Hospitals.<br/><br/>5.	To ensure quality in sterilization services, a nine member Quality Assurance Committee have been setup under the direction of Supreme Court of India at all districts of the country. Its ambit has also been increased to look after quality issues in service delivery in all aspect of Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) programme.<br/><br/>6.	264 backward districts including tribal districts have been identified on the basis of SC/ST population, left wing extremism and low health profile etc for focused monitoring.<br/><br/>7.	As per Rural Health Statistics 2010, there are 26643 Sub Centres, 3742 PHCs and 802 CHCs operational in the country covering the tribal population.  There are 1190 Sub-Centres, 100 PHCs and 5 CHCs operational in the State of Jharkhand to provide healthcare delivery services in tribal areas.<br/><br/>8.	States are provided with Mobile Medical Units and Emergency Referral Transport System to improve the accessibility. 24 districts in the State of Jharkhand are equipped with Mobile Medical Units with 103 vehicles. 166 ambulances are also operational in the State to provide emergency referral services.<br/><br/>9.	A new initiative, Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) recently launched under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) entitles all pregnant women accessing public health institutions, completely free and cashless deliveries including free medicine with zero out of pocket expenses. <br/><br/>10.	 Promotion of institutional delivery through Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) by providing cash assistance to pregnant women especially those who belong to Scheduled Tribes, Scheduled Castes and BPL category. As a result there has been substantial increase in the number of institutional deliveries in the country. The institutional delivery in the State of Jharkhand has increased from 52293 in 2005-06 to 3.45 lakhs in 2010-11.<br/>.........<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Classification of coal mining areas
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) the details of the issue of Go-No-GO classification of coal mining areas;<br/>(b) whether there has been difference of opinion between the Ministry of Coal and the Ministry on this issue; <br/>(c) if so, the details thereof;<br/>(d) whether these differences have been ironed out; and <br/>(e) if so, the latest position on this issue?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT & FORESTS <br/><br/>(SHRIMATI JAYANTHI NATARAJAN)<br/><br/><br/>(a)To facilitate objective, informed and transparent decision on diversion of forest land for coal mining projects, Ministry of Environment & Forests (MoEF) on the suggestion from the Ministry of Coal  jointly undertaken a study in nine major coal fields, namely the Talcher, IB Valley, Mandiraigarh, Sohagpur, Wardha, Singrauli, North Karanpura, West Bokaro and Hasdeo and the coal blocks located in these coalfields were classified into following two categories:<br/><br/>(a)Unfragmented forest landscapes having gross forest cover (GFC) more than 30 percent and weighted forest cover (WFC) more than 10 percent, named as category-A or ‘No-Go’ area.<br/>(b)Fragmented forest landscapes having GFC less than 30 % and WFC less than 10%, named as category-B or ‘Go’ area.<br/>Detail of extent of area covered under the said study and the area classified as ‘Go’ and ‘No-Go’ etc. is annexed.<br/> <br/>(b) to (e) The Ministry of Coal is of the view that the MoEF should consider all coal blocks without reference to Go- No Go areas, as per the current statutes and stipulations for according forest clearances. The MoEF is however, of the view that classification of coal blocks into ‘Go’ –‘No Go’ category, though has only indicative value, the exercise undertaken by the MoEF on the initiative of Ministry of Coal has clearly prioritized the forest areas that may be considered for diversion for coal mining by causing least possible damage to the forests and wildlife and hence, it needs to be taken into account while granting approvals under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.<br/><br/>The Cabinet Committee on Infrastructure while considering the note dated 26.11.2010 and supplementary note dated 10.12.2010 from the Ministry of Coal regarding “Need for making available more coal bearing areas for enhancing coal production” in its meeting held on 13.01.2011, directed that all pertinent issues may, in the first instance, be considered by a Group of Ministers (GoM), and thereafter, the matter be brought before the Committee. The Cabinet Secretariat vide their Memorandum dated 3rd February 2011 constituted a GoM under the Chairmanship of Shri Pranab Mukherjee, Minister of Finance. Matter is still under consideration of the GoM.<br/><br/><br/>******** <br/>

records.qtitle: Setting up of IID centres
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	the number of the Integrated Infrastructure Development (IID) centres functioning in the country at present, State-wise;<br/><br/>(b)	whether Government proposes to set up more IIDs centres in the country;<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(d)	the amount of funds likely to be spent thereon; and<br/><br/>(e)	the details of packages/assistances provided to various States including Jharkhand to strengthen the small scale sector and enhance the competitiveness both domestically and globally? <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF MICRO, SMALL & MEDIUM ENTERPRISES<br/>(SHRI VIRBHADRA SINGH)<br/><br/><br/>(a):	102 Infrastructure Development Centres are functioning in the country, supported under Micro and Small Enterprises – Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP). Details are given at Annexure-I <br/><br/>(b):	Yes, Sir.<br/> <br/>(c):	29 ID Centres are under various stages of implementation. Details given at Annexure-II<br/> <br/>(d):	The amount of funds likely to be spent is given at Annexure-II.<br/>   <br/>(e):	The Government is implementing various schemes / programmes for promotion and development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) for all the states including Jharkhand. The major schemes include Credit Guarantee Scheme, Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme, Performance and Credit Rating Scheme, Cluster Development Programme, National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme and Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme.  In addition, Government announced “Package on Promotion of Micro and Small Enterprises” on 27.2.07, which, inter-alia, provide for credit support, fiscal support, support for cluster based development through technology and quality upgradation, marketing, entrepreneurial and managerial development and strengthening of data base for MSME Sector.  <br/><br/>The Government has also announced ‘North-East Industrial Investment Policy and Promotion (NEIIPP) – 2007’ a package of fiscal incentives and other concessions for all Industrial units in North–East Region States. Transport Subsidy Schemes is being implemented w.e.f. 23.7.1971 in NER States (including Sikkim), Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Darjeeling District in West Bengal, Union Territories of Lakshdweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.   Fiscal incentives for the State of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh are being provided to eligible industrial units w.e.f. 7.1.03.  A special package of incentive is being provided to eligible industrial units in the State of Jammu & Kashmir w.e.f. 14.6.02.<br/>

records.qtitle: Digitizing cable TV system
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	the socio-economic implications of Government’s ordinance for digitizing cable TV system; and<br/><br/>(b)	to what extent it would inflict an additional burden on cable TV operator and customers?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI C. M. JATUA)<br/><br/>(a)	      With the digitization of cable TV system, the service providers will be able to carry large number of TV channels in their network, as compared to those presently carried by analog cable TV system.  Besides, the digital cable TV network has enhanced capability to carry additional innovative services like triple play with broadband, value added service and interactive services such as video-on-demand, gaming etc.  With the addressability, the broadcaster would be able to carry on their business transaction on auditable and verifiable subscriber bases instead of negotiated bases. With the provisions of addressability the consumer will be able to choose the channels of their choice on a-la-carte basis and pay only for the channels subscribed. This will enable the consumers to budget their bill as per choice and affordability. The implementation of digital addressable Cable TV system will bring about complete transparency in business transactions in the sector which in turn will ensure that tax collection by the Government matches to the market size. It will also ensure increased service tax revenue through enhanced deployment of triple play including broadband and other value added services that are possible in the addressable digital Cable TV system.<br/><br/>(b)	    For implementation of Digital Addressable Cable TV System, the cable operators (MSOs/LCOs) may be required to upgrade their distribution network. The MSOs may be required to upgrade their headend equipment whereas the LCOs may be required to upgrade their cable network, in case the existing cable network does not support the services offered in the digital addressable systems. <br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>	    To facilitate the implementation of the digital addressable system, TRAI in its recommendation dated 5th August 2010, has recommended various fiscal incentives such as tax holidays, reduction of custom duties on headend equipment and STBs to zero. Besides, TRAI has also recommended for granting of Right of Way (RoW) permission for laying of cables by the cable operators, on non exclusive basis. As far as consumers are concerned STB will be required for reception of channels as well as other services. In this regard TRAI in its tariff order dated 21st July, 2010 for addressable systems made it mandatory for the cable TV operators to offer the STB on rental, hire-purchase and outright purchase basis so that the consumer may choose the offer most suitable/ affordable to him.<br/>*****<br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(Dr. D. PURANDESWARI)<br/><br/>(a)& (b):	The Government receives grievances regarding the Right of the Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 relating  inter alia to denial of admission, charging of fees, conducting screening tests, expulsion, detention, corporal punishment, lack of basic amenities in school, etc., which are forwarded to the State Governments for appropriate action.<br/>(c) & (d):	Under the RTE Act, the local authority, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) and the State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR) have been entrusted with the responsibility to monitor the rights of the child. The Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) Framework for implementation of the RTE Act provides for establishing a well defined institutional mechanism for grievance redressal involving a system of registering, investigating and responding within a well-appointed time frame and the modalities within which grievances can be dealt with.  <br/>

records.qtitle: Solution of border dispute with China
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: SOLUTION OF BORDER DISPUTE WITH CHINA <br/><br/>1751. 	SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	the details of border disputes between India and China;<br/>(b)	whether a high degree of mistrust continues between the two countries mainly due to territorial disputes; and<br/>(c)	if so, the steps taken to solve these disputes?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI E. AHAMED)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c) China disputes the international boundary between India and China. Indian territory under the occupation by China in Jammu & Kashmir is approximately 38,000 sq. kms. In addition, under the so-called China-Pakistan “Boundary Agreement” signed between China and Pakistan on 2 March 1963, Pakistan illegally ceded 5,180 sq. kms. of Indian territory in Pakistan Occupied Kashmir to China. In the Eastern Sector, China claims approximately 90,000 square kilometers of Indian territory in the State of Arunachal Pradesh. In 2003, India and China agreed to each appoint a Special Representative to explore from the political perspective of the overall bilateral relationship the framework for a boundary settlement. There have been fourteen meetings of the Special Representatives so far. The first five meetings resulted in the signing of the “Agreement on the Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for the Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question” on 11 April 2005. At present the two Special Representatives are exploring the framework for a settlement covering all sectors of the boundary. The two sides have reiterated, on many occasions, their commitment to maintain peace and tranquility along the Line of Actual Control in the India-China border areas, pending a final settlement of the Boundary Question and have put in place various Confidence Building Measures to this end. <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Crash of MIG 29 near Rohtang Pass
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) whether a MIG-29 fighter plane of the Indian Air Force was crashed near Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh recently; if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b)  the route-wise and location-wise number of accidents involving MIG-29 during 2011;<br/><br/>(c) whether any detailed study has been made to identify reasons for MIG crashes in recent past; if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(d)  the steps taken to avoid such mishaps?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):  Yes, Sir.  A MIG-29 fighter plane of the Indian Air Force (IAF) crashed near Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh on 18.10.2011.  The pilot was killed in the crash.  No other MIG-29 aircraft crash occurred during 2011 (up to 1.12.2011).<br/><br/>(c) & (d):  Every IAF aircraft accident is thoroughly investigated by a Court of Inquiry (CoI) to ascertain the cause of accident and remedial measures are taken accordingly to check their recurrence in future.  IAF has taken various measures relating to invigoration of aviation safety organization, analytical studies and quality audits of the aircraft fleets to identify vulnerable areas and institute remedial measures to reduce aircraft accidents.  Ornithology cell, which carries out bird surveys at flying bases and suggests bird prevention modules, has been established at the Directorate of Aerospace Safety.  All flying bases have been visited by senior Aerospace Safety personnel of the IAF to apprise and caution the operating units about the causes of the accidents and to get views towards enhancing aviation safety.  Accident prevention programmes have been given added thrust to identify risk prone/hazardous areas specific to the aircraft fleets and operational environment to ensure safe practices/procedures.  Steps have been taken by the Government to train pilots to prevent accidents due to human error.  These include increased use of simulators to practice procedures and emergency actions, focused and realistic training with additional emphasis on the critical aspects of mission, introduction of Crew Resource Management and Operational Risk Management to enable safe mission launches, Aviation Psychology courses and introduction of Aerospace Safety capsules in the ab initio training of air crew.<br/>

records.qtitle: Availability of coal for power plants
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the Ministry has anticipated shortage in supply of coal for power plants commissioned/to be commissioned during<br/>2011-12;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether owing to shortage of coal, power plants may not operate during 2010-11 and 2011-12;<br/><br/>(c) 	if so, the reasons for this state of affairs; and<br/><br/>(d) 	the steps taken by Government to ensure smooth running of the thermal power plants in 2010-11?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER<br/>( SHRI K.C. VENUGOPAL )<br/><br/>(a) :   		Depending upon the availability of indigenous coal, shortage of coal is estimated on a year to year basis.  For the year 2011-12, against an estimated coal requirement of 455 Million Tonne(MT), availability of indigenous coal was indicated as 402 MT, thereby resulting in a shortfall of 53 MT coal. <br/>(b) & (c) :	No operating thermal power station reported shut down due to non-availability of coal during 2010-11 and 2011-12.  Main reasons for short supply of coal during the current year are:<br/>(i)	Less transportation of coal from coal mines to railway sidings.<br/><br/>(ii)	Inadequate crushing capacity at the coal mines.<br/>(iii)	Law and order problems in the Central Coalfields Limited and  Mahanadi Coalfields Limited.<br/>………2.<br/><br/>- 2 -<br/><br/>(iv)	Reduction in coal production in SCCL due to worker’s strike during September – October, 2011.<br/>(v)	Excessive rains of the coal fields of Northern Coalfields Limited, Central Coalfields Limited and Mahanadi Coalfields Limited.<br/><br/>(d) :	Following steps have been taken by the Government to augment supply of coal to thermal power stations :<br/><br/>(i)	Ministry of Coal/ Coal India Ltd. (CIL) is being insisted upon to enhance production of domestic coal in the country.  <br/><br/>(ii)	Power Utilities are being advised to import coal to bridge the shortfall between requirement of coal and its availability from the domestic sources.<br/><br/>(iii)	The coal supply position is reviewed at various levels in Ministry of Coal, Ministry of Power and Cabinet Secretariat with participation from the concerned Ministries, CEA, Coal India Limited and NTPC.<br/><br/><br/>**********   <br/>

records.qtitle: Delay in infrastructural core sector industries
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	the number of infrastructure core sector industries that have been delayed beyond a decade;<br/><br/>(b)	the amount of cost escalations due to the delays;<br/><br/>(c)	the main factors leading for their delay; and<br/><br/>(d)	the manner in which Government proposes to get rid of these factors and ensure timely completion of projects?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE),  MINISTRY OF    STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI SRIKANT KUMAR JENA)<br/><br/><br/>(a)	As on 31st August, 2011,  out of 553 central sector projects costing Rs. 150 crore and above on the monitor of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, only 3 projects were delayed beyond a decade.  <br/> <br/>(b)	The amount of cost escalation due to this delay is to the tune of Rs.17,999.65 crore;<br/><br/>(c)	The main factors leading for their delay include; delay in land acquisition, delay in procurement of equipment, law and order problems, inadequate infrastructure, delay in mobilization by contractors, general cost escalation due to delay, increase in prices of cement and steel and exchange rate variations.<br/><br/>(d)	In order to reduce the delays and ensure timely completion of these projects, the Government has already taken several steps which inter-alia include :<br/><br/>•	Stricter appraisal of projects by way of inter-ministry  consultations and adoption of two-stage clearance system, first by PIB/EFC, secondly by CCI/CCEA.<br/>•	Monthly monitoring of output/ performance of infrastructure Ministries by MOSPI;<br/>•	Monthly and quarterly monitoring of time & cost overrun of projects costing      Rs. 150 crores and above by MOSPI;  <br/>•	In-depth review of projects on  quarterly basis by the concerned infrastructure Ministries;<br/>•	Follow up with the State Governments in respect of problems relating to land acquisition, rehabilitation related issues, forest clearances, environment/ wildlife clearances, removal of encroachments & availability of Right of Way (ROW), ensuring law and order at project sites, etc. This Ministry has already advised the states to constitute the Central Sector Projects Coordination Committee (CSPCC) under respective Chief Secretaries to facilitate Central Sector Projects in the states and 13 states have since constituted the Coordination Committee in their respective States.<br/>•	Faster appraisal through Departmental Committees like Expanded Board of Railways in lieu of PIB;<br/>•	Setting up of Standing Committees by the Government in the Ministries/Departments headed by respective Additional Secretaries to fix responsibility for time and cost overruns;<br/>•	Appointment of nodal officers for each project with continuity of tenure; <br/>•	Adoption of computer network based monitoring; and<br/>•	Organising training courses and seminars on project planning, monitoring and project management for project managers of CPSUs by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation:<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Implementation status of NRHM
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: GOVERNMENT OF INDIA<br/>MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE<br/>DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE<br/><br/>RAJYA  SABHA<br/>UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.866<br/>TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 29th NOVEMBER, 2011<br/>IMPLEMENTATION STATUS OF NRHM<br/><br/>866. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) the target set under National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) in the country during the Eleventh Five Year Plan;<br/><br/>(b) how far the targets have been achieved during the first three years of the<br/>Plan;<br/><br/>(c) the States which have performed above national average and those which could not perform well in NRHM; and<br/><br/>(d) the steps taken for better implementation of NRHM in backward States?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI SUDIP BANDHYOPADHYAY)<br/><br/>(a) The targets set under NRHM are: to reduce the Infant Mortality Rate(IMR) to 30 per 1000 live births, to reduce the Maternal Mortality Ratio(MMR) to 100 per 100,000 live births, to reduce Total Fertility Rate(TFR) to 2.1.<br/>     (b)  As per Sample Registration System (SRS) bulletin published by Registrar General of India, the IMR has reduced from 57 per 1000 live births in 2006 to 50 per 1000 live births in 2009. The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) has reduced from 2.8 in 2006 to 2.6 in 2009. The Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) has declined from 254 during 2004-06 to 212 during 2007-09. <br/>(c)	A statement showing State-wise details of IMR, MMR and TFR including National average is placed at Annexure. <br/><br/>(d)	Steps taken for better implementation of NRHM in backward states inter-alia include:<br/><br/>i.	264 backward districts identified across the country for differential financing and focused attention.<br/>ii.	A new initiative, Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) recently launched under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) which, entitles all pregnant women accessing public health institutions completely free and cashless deliveries including free medicine with zero out of pocket expenses.  <br/><br/>iii.	To overcome shortage of Specialists, Multi skilling of the available doctors through trainings such as Life Saving Anesthetic Skills(LSAS), Basic Emergency Obstetrics & Neonatal Care (BeMONC), Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric & Neonatal Care (CeMONC) taken up.<br/><br/>iv.	To improve availability of personnel in difficult and remote areas, monetary incentives are provided to staff posted in such hard to reach and inaccessible areas.<br/><br/>v.	Allowing contractual appointment under NRHM to immediately fill gaps so as to meet the requirement of manpower. 1.46 lakhs health personnel including doctors, specialists, nurses and paramedics have been engaged under NRHM.<br/><br/>vi.	Over 8 lakhs Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) have been engaged to bridge the gap between community and health facilities.<br/><br/>vii.	States are provided with assistance to operate Mobile Medical Units and Emergency Referral Transport System. <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Increasing cost of medical treatment
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: GOVERNMENT OF INDIA<br/>MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/><br/> RAJYA  SABHA<br/>UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.843<br/>TO BE ANSWERED ON 29TH  NOVEMBER, 2011<br/>  <br/>INCREASING COST OF MEDICAL TREATMENT<br/><br/>843. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/>(a) whether it is a fact that public spending on health in India is almost the<br/>lowest in the world;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the steps taken by Government at the Central and State levels to improve health related infrastructure in the country; and<br/><br/>(c) the manner in which the Centre proposes to manage the contradiction of<br/>health and medical services becoming costlier day-by-day for the common man<br/>of the country in the face of promotion of medical tourism by some State<br/>Governments?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)<br/><br/>(a)	According to World Health Statistics-2011 published by World Health Organisation (WHO), the public health expenditure as percentage of GDP for India in 2008 is 1.36%, as compared to public expenditure on health in respect of some select countries, e.g.  China: 2.03%, Bangladesh 1.04%, Pakistan: 0.84%, Sri Lanka 1.79%, Indonesia: 1.25%, in 2008. <br/><br/>(b) & (c):  Under National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) financial assistance has been provided to the States for augmentation of human resources for health sector, improvement of infrastructure of public health care facilities, provision of drug and equipment, setting up of Mobile Medical Units to serve people in the far flung areas, provision of Emergency and Referral transport etc.  The Mission also provides Untied Funds, Annual Maintenance Grants and Rogi Kalyan Samiti funds for various public health facilities to  provide better  health services.<br/><br/>The other measures taken inter-alia include: <br/>•	 Making available specialized health care services through strengthening of hospitals. <br/>•	Setting up of AIIMS like medical Institutions/strengthening of Government medical colleges in different States. <br/>All these steps are expected to improve health related infrastructure in the country and to provide accessible, affordable, accountable, effective and quality healthcare services, especially to the poor and vulnerable sections of population of the country. <br/>

records.qtitle: Supply of required quantity of coal to power plants
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the Coal India Ltd (CIL) is not in a position to supply the required coal for power plants in the country; <br/><br/>(b)	if so, the magnitude of this shortage ; <br/><br/>(c)      the reasons for not being able to supply the required quantity; and <br/><br/>(d)    	the quality and value of coal required to be imported to bridge the gap; and<br/><br/>(e)	how far environmental considerations are responsible for the shortage of coal threatening operationalisation of power projects?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE  IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL  <br/>(SHRI  PRATIK PRAKASHBAPU PATIL  )<br/>(a) to (c):	During the last three years, the coal despatches by Coal India Limited (CIL) to the  Power Utilities were  102%, 96% and 91% of targets fixed for 2008-09, 2009-10 & 2010-11 respectively. Despatches during 2009-10 and 2010-11 were less than the target, mainly due to frequent law and order problems particularly in Jharkhand and Odisha affecting coal despatches in Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL), Central Coalfields Limited (CCL) & Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) and constraints of wagon availability in comparison to indents in certain coal fields.  <br/><br/> 	During 2011-12, upto October,2011, coal dispatch from CIL coal companies to the power utilities was 91% of the pro-rata  target, committed under the Fuel Supply Agreement / Memorandum of Understanding.  Coal dispatches to power stations went down during the second quarter of this year mainly due to heavy rains in the coalfields during August/September, severely affecting transportation and wagon loading. <br/><br/>…2/-<br/><br/>-	2  -<br/>Despatch was also hampered due to unloading constraints of a few power stations and stoppage of lifting through private washeries by MAHAGENCO power stations. <br/>(d):	 As per the assessment made by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), the coal requirement for the power plants designed on indigenous coal has been estimated at 457 Million Tonnes during 2011-12.  Against this requirement, the coal availability from the indigenous sources has been estimated at 405 Million Tonnes and the balance has to be met through imports by power utilities.  Ministry of Power has fixed import target of 35 Million Tonnes, which is considered equivalent to about 52 Million Tonnes of indigenous coal due to higher calorific value of imported coal, for import by the power utilities during 2011-12.  The power utilities require “F” grade non-coking coal which needs to be imported by them, but the value of coal to be imported by the power utilities cannot be estimated at this stage.<br/>(e):	Issues relating to delay in land acquisition,  obtaining statutory clearances relating to environment / forest, Rehabilitation and Resettlement issues etc have resulted in reduced coal production targets by CIL. While finalizing the 11th Plan document, it was estimated that the coal production target for CIL, by the end of terminal year of 11th Plan ( 2011-12) would be 520 Million Tonnes, but it had to be revised downwards  to 447 Million Tonnes due to the above mentioned reasons. The reduced availability of coal from CIL sources is affecting all consumers, including the power utilities.  <br/>*******<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Viability of fair price shops
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the economic viability of Fair Price Shops (FPSs) has been badly affected by exclusion of APL population from PDS;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether only 23 per cent FPSs viable in terms of earning a return of 12 percent on capital;<br/><br/>(d) 	whether this has not encouraged instances of cheating by FPS owners; and<br/><br/>(e) 	the steps taken to make FPS economically viable?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) to (e):   Government allocates foodgrains (rice and wheat)  @ 35 kg. per family per month to States/Union Territories (UTs) for 6.52 crore accepted number of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families, which includes about 2.44 crore Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) families, for distribution at subsidized prices through Fair Price Shops (FPSs). Allocation of foodgrains to about 11.52 crore Above Poverty Line (APL) families are also made depending upon the availability of foodgrains in the central pool and the past offtake. Presently, the allocation of foodgrains to APL families ranges between 15 and 35 kg per family per month.                 <br/>               <br/>In the report of the Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) of the Planning Commission on Performance Evaluation of  Targeted Public Distribution System(TPDS)  (March, 2005), it was mentioned that only about 22.7% of the FPSs were found to be earning a return of 12% on capital.  Various evaluation studies of TPDS have recommended door-step delivery of TPDS items, permitting the sale of non-PDS commodities, higher margins for FPS owners, etc. for  making the FPSs more viable.<br/>             <br/>During the Conference of States/UTs held in July, 2010, it was resolved among others that States will endeavour to ensure door-step delivery of foodgrains to FPSs. State/UT Governments have also been given flexibility in the matter of fixing the margin for FPSs.  The end retail prices of foodgrains at FPSs are fixed by the State/UT Governments keeping in view the margin/commission paid to FPS dealers, transportation charges, etc.  However, the end retails price for AAY families is to be retained at Rs.2/- per kg for wheat and Rs.3/- per kg for rice.  In addition, State/UT Governments have been advised that FPS owners should be encouraged to enlarge the basket of commodities by adding non-PDS items for sale through these outlets.  Some of the State/UTs have reported distribution of non-PDS items like pulses, edible oils, iodized salt, spices, etc. through PDS outlets.<br/><br/><br/>****<br/>

records.qtitle: Trade value in commodity exchanges
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text: (a)  	whether the average daily value of trade in the commodity exchanges doubled during 2008-09;<br/>(b)  	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c)  	the share of agricultural commodities in the increase; and<br/>(d)  	how far this increase has been responsible for increase in food inflation?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) & (b):	No, Sir. The average daily value of trade in the commodity exchanges increased by 27% in 2008-09 over the value of trade in 2007-08.  The average daily value of trade in 2007-2008 was recorded at Rs.13,374.96 crores and the corresponding figure for 2008-2009 was Rs.17,042.06 crores. <br/><br/>(c)	:	The share of agricultural commodities in total value of trade declined from 23.15% in 2007-2008 to 11.95% in 2008-2009.<br/><br/>(d)	:	According to available information there is no clear evidence that rise in food prices in India has been due to forward trading.  Futures trading only discovers futures prices based on expected demand-supply of the commodity. An Expert Committee of the Planning Commission that analyzed annual growth rate in prices of sensitive commodities (food grains and sugar) in pre- futures and post  futures period,  concluded that although inflation clearly increased  post-futures  in some  sensitive  commodities that have higher  weight in  consumer price  indices, it is  not  possible to make any  general claim that inflation accelerated more in commodities with futures trading. 	In essence, other factors particularly demand supply mismatches, degree of dependence on imports and international prices in these commodities etc. tend to affect commodity prices.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Teachers education
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	whether teachers’ education is one of the major schemes under elementary education in the country;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the objectives of the scheme;<br/><br/>(c) 	how far these objectives have been achieved;<br/><br/>(d) 	what has been the performance of different States;<br/><br/>(e) 	whether in a recent examination conducted in Bihar for primary school teachers, the result have been poor; and <br/><br/> (f) 	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(Dr. D. PURANDESWARI)<br/><br/>(a) & (b)	The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Teacher Education provides academic resource support to elementary and secondary teachers through training, action research and experimentation, and developing decentralized institutional structures for pre-service and in-service teacher training. Under the Scheme, the Central Government provides resource support to the State Governments for establishment and functioning of District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs), strengthening of secondary teacher education institutions into Colleges of Teacher Education (CTEs) and Institutes of Advanced Study in Education (IASEs) and strengthening of the State Councils of Educational Research and Training (SCERTs).<br/><br/><br/>(c) & (d)	Since inception of the Teacher Education Scheme in 1987, 571 DIETs, 106 CTEs and 32 IASEs have been sanctioned in various States/UTs.  State-wise position is given in the Annexure. The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), New Delhi in its Report on Comprehensive Evaluation of the Teacher Education Scheme (August, 2009) has reported that the institutions of DIETs, CTEs and IASEs have played a pivotal role in providing pre-service and in-service training of teachers and teacher educators as an important quality input for school education in the country. However, the performance of these institutions has been uneven across States, with States such as Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh having shown relatively better performance than some other States such as Bihar and Jharkhand.<br/>(e) & (f)	The Government of Bihar has informed that it had conducted Teachers’ Achievement Tests in 2009 and 2010 in which the percentage of teachers who were successful was 83.52 and 90.38, respectively.<br/>

records.qtitle: Pupil  Teacher ratio
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)	the ideal pupil-teacher ratio for primary and upper Primary school levels;<br/>(b)	the pupil-teacher ratio at present;<br/>(c)	how far the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan has been able to bring an improvement in the pupil-teacher ratio; and <br/>(d)	the position so far as Jharkhand is concerned?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(Dr. D. PURANDESWARI)<br/><br/><br/>(a):	The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which became operative with effect from 1st April, 2010, prescribes that Pupil- Teacher Ratio (PTR) in schools should be maintained as per the following specified levels:<br/>A.	For classes I to V:<br/>(i)	Two teachers for up to sixty admitted children<br/>(ii)	Three teachers for 61-90 children<br/>(iii)	Four teachers for 91-120 children<br/>(iv)	Five teachers for 121-200 children<br/>(v)	One Head Teacher, other than the five teachers, if the number of admitted 	children exceeds 150; and the PTR (excluding Head Teacher) shall not 	exceed forty if the number of admitted children is above 200.<br/><br/>B.	For Classes VI to VIII:<br/>(i)	At least one teacher per class so that there shall be at least one teacher each for (a) Science and Mathematics; (b) Social Studies; and (c) Languages.<br/>(ii)	At least one teacher for every 35 children;<br/>(iii)	Where admission of children is above 100, there shall be (a) a full time head-teacher and (b) part time instructors for Art Education, Health & Physical Education and Work Education.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):	Since inception of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) in 2001-02, 19.14 lakh posts of teachers have been sanctioned till October, 2011.   The PTR at National level has improved from 36 at Elementary level in 2005-06  to 33 and 31 at Primary and Upper Primary level respectively as per District Information System for Education (DISE) – 2009-10. <br/><br/>(d):	In respect of Jharkhand, the PTR is 45 and 47 at Primary and Upper Primary level, respectively as per DISE- 2009-10.  <br/>

records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE <br/>MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/>(SHRI JITIN PRASADA)<br/><br/>(a) and  (b )	This Ministry is primarily responsible for the development and maintenance of National Highways (NHs) and the roads other than NHs are responsibility of the concerned State Governments, etc.  Apart from this, the Ministry also allocates funds to the States for development of State Roads under the Central Road Fund (CRF) and Economic Importance (EI) & Inter-State Connectivity (ISC) schemes.<br/>	<br/>The development of NHs is a continuous process and the works are, accordingly, taken up based on the traffic density, inter-se priority and availability of funds.  However, about 32,754 km length of NHs is programmed to be developed to 4 or more lane NH standards under various phases of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP). Besides these programmes, development works on NHs including widening of NHs are also taken up under National Highway (Original) [NH(O)] under Annual Plan.<br/><br/><br/><br/>(c ) and (d)	Targets fixed for development of NHs and other roads under various programmes such as NHDP, SARDP-NE including Arunachal Pradesh Package and Special Programme for development of roads in the LWE affected areas are given below:<br/><br/>Sl. No. 			Category 				Target during 2011-12<br/>			 (km)<br/>I.	National Highways Development Project (NHDP)		2,500<br/>II.	Others Programmes	<br/>	(a) Special Accelerated Road Development Programme in the North East (SARDP-NE) including Arunachal Pradesh Package 		270<br/>	(b) Special Programme for development of Roads in the Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected areas 		800<br/><br/>	The State-wise details of targets fixed for the development of NHs under NH(O) during 2011-12 are annexed.  <br/><br/>The various measures taken for expeditious implementation of the National Highway projects include regular monitoring at various levels, appointment of nodal officer in each State for coordinating land acquisition, shifting of utilities and obtaining various clearances, simplification of process of issue of notification for land acquisition, grant of advances to the contractors and punitive action against non-performing contractors, etc.<br/>

records.qtitle: Social security schemes for workers in unorganised sector
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: 278. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:<br/>	<br/>(a)the magnitude of the workers working in the unorganised/informal sector as well as the workers employed in an informal capacity in the organised sector;<br/>(b)whether this category of work force is excluded from the institutionalised social security cover; and<br/>(c)if so, the reasons for not providing them with the required social security schemes?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>(SHRI MALLIKARJUN KHARGE)<br/><br/>(a):		According to the survey conducted by National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) in 2004-05, 433 million workers were in the unorganized sector which constituted about 94% of the total labour force.<br/>(b) & (c):	Recognizing the need of providing social security to unorganised workers, irrespective of their informal or formal capacity, the Government has enacted the Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act 2008. The Act provides for constitution of Nation Social Security Board to recommend social security schemes viz. life and disability cover, health maternity benefits, old age protection and any other benefit as may be determined by the Government for unorganized workers.<br/>Contd….2/-<br/>::  2  ::<br/><br/>The Government launched the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana for BPL families (a unit of five) in unorganized sector on 01.10.2007. The scheme providing for smart card based cashless health insurance cover of Rs. 30,000/- per family per annum on a family floater basis, became operational form 01.04.2008. More than 2.51 crore families have been covered under the scheme as on 31.10.2011.<br/><br/>To provide death and disability cover to rural landless households between the age group of the 18 to 59 years, the Government launched the ‘Aam Admi Bima Yojana’ on 02.10.2007 More than 1.78 crore lives have been covered under the scheme as on 31.07.2011.<br/><br/>Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme provides for old age pension of Rs.200 per month to persons above the age of 60 years. For the persons above the age of 80 years the amount of pension has been raised to Rs.500 per month.<br/><br/>The Government is implementing various other employment generation/social security schemes for workers in the unorganised sector, such as Swarnjayanti Gram Swarojgar Yojana, Swarn Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yogana, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme, Mahatama Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, Handloom Weavers’ comprehensive Welfare Schemes, Handicraft Artisans’ comprehensive Welfare Schemes, Pension to Mastercraftpersons, National Scheme for Welfare of Fishermen and Training and Extension, Janani Surkasha Yojana, National Family Benefits Scheme, Janshree Bima Yojana New Pension Schemes (Swavalamban  scheme) through various Ministries/Departments.<br/><br/>The Government has constituted Welfare Fund to provide welfare measures to the beedi workers and their family members. These include health care, housing assistance, education to children and group insurance etc.<br/>

records.qtitle: Proposal to increase employment in organised sector
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: 277.	 SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI :   <br/><br/>Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	whether as per a recent National Sample Survey over half of India’s workface is self-employed;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c)	whether as per this Survey only 16 per cent are regular wage or salaried employees;<br/>(d)	if so, the reason for a small number of workers in the organised sector; and<br/>(e)	whether Government propose to increase employment in the organised sector?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>(SHRI MALLIKARJUN KHARGE)<br/><br/>(a)	Yes, Sir.<br/>(b)	51% workforce is engaged in self-employment in the country based on the results of the survey conducted by National Sample Survey Office during 2009-10. <br/>(c)	 to (e) Yes, Sir. Employment has been growing in the organized sector slowly. However, the Eleventh Plan aims at increasing private organized sector employment ambitiously, by at least 10 million. Along with the public sector, organized sector jobs would then expand by over 15 million, a growth rate of about 9% per annum.<br/>

records.qtitle: Anti inflationary measures by RBI
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text: (a)whether the anti-inflationary measures taken by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) have failed to make the desired effect;<br/><br/>(b)if not, how far these have been successful in controlling the inflation;<br/><br/>(c)the impact of trading off higher inflation for higher growth in the long run; and <br/><br/>(d)how the detrimental effects thereof, if any, will be countered?
records.ans_text: FINANCE MINISTER<br/>(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)<br/><br/>(a)to (d):  A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO<br/>RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 15 <br/>BY SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI<br/>REGARDING ANTI-INFLATIONARY MEASURES BY RBI<br/>DUE FOR ANSWER ON NOVEMBER 22, 2011<br/>               ......<br/><br/>(a)&(b): Monetary policy measures have helped contain inflation and anchor inflationary expectations, although both remain at an elevated level. However, the task of monetary management was rendered difficult due to the nature of food inflation, uncertain global environment and rise in global commodity prices.<br/><br/>(c)&(d): High inflation and also some of the effort to control liquidity has detrimental effect on short run growth. The immediate priority is to control inflation so that long term growth prospects are not affected.<br/>                     *****

records.qtitle: Environmental Clearance to POSCO

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT & FORESTS <br/><br/>(SHRIMATI JAYANTHI NATARAJAN)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) The Ministry of Environment and Forests had accorded stage-II approval under the Forests (Conservation) Act, 1980 for diversion of 1253.225 hectares of forest land for establishment of an integrated steel plant and captive port by M/s. Ltd. shall take up afforestation inside the forest area in 100 meter radius from the permitted lease area in consultation with the Forest Department; and<br/><br/>(vii)User agency would bear the cost of regeneration of an equivalent amount of open, degraded forest land in a district to be determined and indicated by the State Government of Orissa.<br/><br/>*****

(c): The number of FTAs in India, during 2010, for various purposes including rural and health tourism was 5.58 million.

records.qtitle: FUND FOR PANCHAYATS IN JHARRKHAND .
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text:
(a) the fund that is lapsed/remained unutilised because of non existence of Panchayats in Jharkhand since the time of formation of the State;

(b) since the Panchayat Elections in Jharkhand, how much funds have been released to the State;

(c) whether the lapsed amount /unutilised amount can be regranted to the State for the development in a phased manner; ( d) if so, in what manner; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PANCHA YATI RAJ

(SHRI V. KISHORE CHANDRA DEO)

(a) & (b): Central funds for PRIs are released to States through two modes:

(i) Backward Region Grant Fund (BRGF), which is being operated by Ministry of Panchayati Raj in 250 identified districts.

(ii) Finance Commission Grant which is released by Ministry of Finance. The condition for release of fund under BRGF is constitution of District Planning Committee (DPC) and approval of district plan by them, where as the condition for release under Finance Commission is existence of elected Panchayats

in the States. Ministry of Panchayati Raj has relaxed the condition of having DPCs before release of BRGF grant to Jharkhand in 2010-11. However, Ministry of Finance has been insisting the condition of existence of elected Panchayats before release of Finance Commission Grants. The amount Allocated, Released and utilization reported in respect of Jharkhand under BRGF programme and Finance Commissions are at Annxe.

(c) to (e): No, Sir, the lapsed amount/unutilized amount cannot be granted to the State for development in phased manner, because the Grants recommended by the Central Finance Commissions are for the durations of the award period.

records.qtitle: PROTECTING COASTAL AREAS .
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has realized vulnerability of coastal areas of the country, particularly highly industrialized coastal belt of Gujarat, in view of terrorist attacks of 26/11 in Mumbai and recent attacks of 13/7 and how is it planning to protect coastal areas of industrial belts like Jamnagar, Dahej, Hazira and Kutch in Gujarat having vital installations of critical industries established with huge capital outlay;

(b) whether these vital installations of coastal areas of Gujarat are under terror threat;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) what action is being taken by Government to safeguard such vital installations and people in these regions?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN )

(a) Yes, Sir. Subsequent to the Mumbai incident of 26/11, the entire coastal security scenario of the country has been subjected to multi-level, inter-ministerial review by the Government of India and several important decisions/initiatives have been taken. The Indian Navy has been designated as the authority responsible for overall maritime security which includes coastal security and offshore security. The Indian Coast Guard has been additionally designated as the authority responsible for coastal security in territorial waters including areas to be patrolled by Coastal Police. The Director General Coast


Guard has been designated as Commander Coastal Command responsible for overall coordination between Central and State agencies in all matter relating to coastal security.

(b) & (C): inputs continue to indicate threat to vital installations located along with coastal areas of Gujarat.

(d) : security inspection of vital installations is being conducted on regular basis and the management concerned/State Government is also being sensitized to take suitable security measures.

records.qtitle: PROGRESS OF EXCAVATION PROECTS .
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether several excavation projects were undertaken in the country during the Tenth Five Year Plan;

(b) If so, whether Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat ) is one of them ; and

(c) If so, the details of progress made by all the projects including Dholavira so far? A N S W E R
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION AND MINISTER OF CULTURE

(KUMARI SELJA)

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. The details of the excavation undertaken by various agencies during the Tenth Five Year Plan are enclosed at Annexure.

(c) The excavation projects including Dholavira conducted during the period under review have since been completed.

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN PENSION FOR WIDOWS IN BPL CATEGORY .
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of widows of BPL category in the country who get 200 per month as pension under the Government scheme, State-wise;

(b) whether BPL widows are adequately aware of the scheme across India;

(c) whether there is any plan to increase the amount of pension, which is very meagre at present; and

(d) whether Government has any other such scheme for BPL widows?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)


(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 467 for reply on 6th September, 2011

(a): Under Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), 34.25 lakh widows of BPL category in the country are reported to be covered, during the year 2010-11. The number of beneficiaries State-wise, is as in Annexure.

(b): IGNWPS is a component of National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) which is under State Plan w.e.f. 2002-03. Identification of beneficiaries, sanction and disbursement of pension are responsibilities of the State Governments. From the year 2010-11, States have been allowed to incur expenditure up to 3% of the total funds under NSAP, towards administrative expenses including that on Information, Education and Communication (IEC) activities.

(c): No, Sir. At present, there is no proposal to increase the amount of pension under IGNWPS. However, in addition to the Central Assistance, many States are contributing to the pension from their own resources.

(d): The Central Government has no other similar pension scheme for BPL widows. However, some States have their own widow pension schemes, in addition to the IGNWPS, with varying eligibility criteria.

records.qtitle: ATTACHMENT OF BLACK MONEY STASHED ABROAD
records.name: Parimal Nathwani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has entered into agreement with certain countries under which it could attach the black money stashed in their banks by Indian citizens;

(b) if so, the details of such countries; and

(c) the action taken by Government so far in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) & (b) Yes Sir. India has Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) with 80 countries. 28 out of these 80 DTAAs have an article on assistance in collection of taxes. This article provides for assistance by the other country in collection of tax claim originating in India and vice versa. It also includes provision for taking measures of conservancy by the other country. These 28 countries are: Armenia, Bangladesh, Belarus, Belgium, Botswana, Czech Republic, Denmark, Iceland, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Luxembourg, Mexico, Morocco, Mozambique, Norway, Poland, Portuguese Republic, Qatar, Romania, South Africa, Sudan, Sweden, Tajikistan, Trinidad and Tobago, Turkmenistan, Uganda and Ukraine.

(c) As and when request is received from the assessing officer, or the tax recovery officer, the same is forwarded to the other country for collecting tax claim originating in India as well as for taking measures of conservancy, wherever applicable.
